Mahāmaudgalyāyana, if in my True Dharma and Vinaya the noble assembly is pure and does not accept corpses, and if there is someone who is not diligent, who is of evil birth, who is not living the holy life yet claims to live the holy life, who is not a śramaṇa yet claims to be a śramaṇa, although he may remain among the noble assembly, he is far from the noble assembly, and the noble assembly is also far removed from him, this is called an unprecedented quality in my True Dharma and Vinaya.

"Furthermore, Mahāmaudgalyāyana, just as on the continent of Jambudvīpa there are five great rivers: the first is called the Gaṅgā, the second is called the Yamunā, the third is called the Sarabhū, the fourth is called the Airāvatī, and the fifth is called the Mahī. All flow into the great ocean; and also in the great ocean, the dragon waters and the rain falling from the sky, with drops as large as chariot-wheel pins. All this water cannot cause the great ocean to increase or decrease. Mahāmaudgalyāyana, my True Dharma and Vinaya are likewise: when sons of good family from the kṣatriya class shave off their beard and hair, don the kāṣāya robes, and with firm faith leave the household life for the homeless life to train in the Way, attaining the unshakable liberation of mind, realizing it through their own direct knowledge and abiding in its attainment. Mahāmaudgalyāyana, the unshakable liberation of mind, in my True Dharma and Vinaya, causes neither increase nor decrease. Likewise, when sons of good family from the brahmin class, the householder class, and the artisan class shave off their beard and hair, don the kāṣāya robes, and with firm faith leave the household life for the homeless life to train in the Way, attaining the unshakable liberation of mind, realizing it through their own direct knowledge and abiding in its attainment. Mahāmaudgalyāyana, the unshakable liberation of mind, in my True Dharma and Vinaya, causes neither increase nor decrease. Mahāmaudgalyāyana, if in my True Dharma and Vinaya sons of good family from the kṣatriya class shave off their beard and hair, don the kāṣāya robes, and with firm faith leave the household life for the homeless life to train in the Way, attaining the unshakable liberation of mind, realizing it through their own direct knowledge and abiding in its attainment, and the unshakable liberation of mind, in my True Dharma and Vinaya, causes neither increase nor decrease; likewise, when sons of good family from the brahmin class, the householder class, and the artisan class shave off their beard and hair, don the kāṣāya robes, and with firm faith leave the household life for the homeless life to train in the Way, attaining the unshakable liberation of mind, realizing it through their own direct knowledge and abiding in its attainment, and the unshakable liberation of mind, in my True Dharma and Vinaya, causes neither increase nor decrease, this is called an unprecedented quality in my True Dharma and Vinaya."

Thus spoke the Buddha. The Venerable Mahāmaudgalyāyana and the bhikṣus, having heard what the Buddha said, rejoiced and practiced accordingly.

End of the Sixth Sūtra, the Campā Sūtra.

---

## (38) Sūtra of the Householder Ugga, Seventh of the Chapter on Unprecedented Qualities in the Madhyamāgama

Thus have I heard:

At one time, the Buddha was traveling in Vaiśālī, staying in the Great Forest.

At that time, the householder Ugga, attended solely by women, with himself at the forefront of the women, went out from Vaiśālī, and in the area between Vaiśālī and the Great Forest engaged solely in female entertainment and amusement, like a king. Thereupon, the householder Ugga, having drunk much wine and become greatly intoxicated, left the women and went into the Great Forest. The householder Ugga, greatly intoxicated from wine, saw from afar the World-Honored One among the forest trees, handsome and beautiful, like the moon among the stars, with radiance brilliant and dazzling, shining like a golden mountain, complete with all the marks of excellence, majestic in supernatural power, with faculties calm and settled, without any obstruction, having accomplished perfect self-mastery, with mind at rest in silent tranquility. Having seen the Buddha, his intoxication instantly cleared. After the householder Ugga's intoxication had cleared, he went to the Buddha, bowed his head at the Buddha's feet, and sat to one side.

At that time, the World-Honored One taught him the Dharma, arousing his aspiration and thirst, bringing him to accomplishment in joy. With immeasurable skillful means he taught him the Dharma, arousing his aspiration and thirst, bringing him to accomplishment in joy. As is the method of all Buddhas, he first taught the proper Dharma that delights the listener: namely, teaching about generosity, teaching about morality, teaching about rebirth in the heavens; he censured desire as calamitous, birth and death as defilement; he praised desirelessness as sublime, and the factors of the path as pure and white. After the World-Honored One had taught him such Dharma, the Buddha knew that he had a joyful mind, a ready mind, a gentle mind, a receptive mind, a mind inclined upward, a single-pointed mind, a mind free of doubt, a mind free of hindrances, and that he had the ability and the power to receive the True Dharma. As all Buddhas teach the essential True Dharma, the World-Honored One then taught him about suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path. At that time, the householder Ugga, right there on his seat, saw the Four Noble Truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path. Just as a piece of clean white silk is easily dyed with color, so too the householder Ugga, right there on his seat, saw the Four Noble Truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path.

Thereupon, the householder Ugga, having seen the Dharma, obtained the Dharma, realized the pure white Dharma, cut through doubt, crossed beyond perplexity, acknowledged no other teacher, no longer followed others, was without hesitation, had established himself in the fruit of realization, and had attained fearlessness in the World-Honored One's Dharma. He then rose from his seat, bowed to the Buddha, and said: "World-Honored One! I now take refuge in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha of bhikṣus. May the World-Honored One accept me as an upāsaka. From this day forth, I take refuge for life, until the end of my days. World-Honored One! From this day, I take from the World-Honored One the five precepts for the rest of my life, with the holy life as foremost."

After the householder Ugga had taken from the World-Honored One the five precepts for the rest of his life, with the holy life as foremost, he bowed his head at the Buddha's feet, circumambulated him three times, and departed. He returned to his home and immediately gathered together all his wives. Having gathered them, he said: "Do you know? I have taken from the World-Honored One the five precepts for the rest of my life, with the holy life as foremost. If any of you wish to remain here, you may remain here, practicing generosity and making merit. If you do not wish to remain, you may each return to your own families. If any of you wish to be given in marriage, I shall arrange your marriage."

Thereupon, his chief wife said to the householder Ugga: "If you have taken from the Buddha the five precepts for the rest of your life, with the holy life as foremost, then please give me to such-and-such a man."

The householder Ugga then called for that man, and grasping his chief wife's arm with his left hand and holding a golden water vessel in his right hand, he said to that man: "I now give you my chief wife to be your wife."

That man, upon hearing this, was greatly frightened, with hair standing on end all over his body, and said to the householder Ugga: "Householder! Do you wish to kill me? Do you wish to kill me?"

The householder replied: "I do not wish to kill you. However, I have taken from the Buddha the five precepts for the rest of my life, with the holy life as foremost. Therefore I give my chief wife to you to be your wife." After the householder Ugga had given away his chief wife, whether during the giving, at the time of giving, or after the giving, he had no regret whatsoever in his mind.

At that time, the World-Honored One, surrounded by countless hundreds of thousands in the great assembly, praised and commended the householder Ugga, saying that the householder Ugga possessed eight unprecedented qualities.

Thereupon, a certain bhikṣu, the next morning at dawn, donned his robes, took his bowl, and went to the home of the householder Ugga. The householder Ugga saw the bhikṣu coming from afar, immediately rose from his seat, bared one shoulder, and with palms joined toward the bhikṣu, said: "Venerable one, welcome! It has been long since the venerable one came here. Please be seated on this couch." The bhikṣu then sat on the couch. The householder Ugga bowed at the bhikṣu's feet and sat to one side.

The bhikṣu said: "Householder! You have gained good benefit and great merit. Why is this? The World-Honored One, surrounded by countless hundreds of thousands in the great assembly, praised and commended you, saying that the householder Ugga possesses eight unprecedented qualities. Householder, what qualities do you have?"

The householder Ugga replied to the bhikṣu: "Venerable one, the World-Honored One has never spoken falsely. However, I do not know for what reason the World-Honored One said this. But please listen, venerable one, and I shall tell you of the qualities I have. At one time, the World-Honored One was traveling in Vaiśālī, staying in the Great Forest. Venerable one, at that time I was attended solely by women, with myself at the forefront, going out from Vaiśālī, and in the area between Vaiśālī and the Great Forest engaging solely in female entertainment and amusement, like a king. Venerable one, at that time I had drunk much wine and become greatly intoxicated, left the women and went into the Great Forest. Venerable one, at that time, greatly intoxicated, I saw from afar the World-Honored One among the forest trees, handsome and beautiful, like the moon among the stars, with radiance brilliant and dazzling, shining like a golden mountain, complete with all the marks of excellence, majestic in supernatural power, with faculties calm and settled, without any obstruction, having accomplished perfect self-mastery, with mind at rest in silent tranquility. Having seen the Buddha, my intoxication instantly cleared. Venerable one, this is one quality I have."

The bhikṣu exclaimed: "Householder! If you have such a quality, how extraordinary! How remarkable!"

"Venerable one, I do not only have this quality. Furthermore, venerable one, after my intoxication cleared, I went to the Buddha, bowed my head at the Buddha's feet, and sat to one side. The World-Honored One taught me the Dharma, arousing my aspiration and thirst, bringing me to accomplishment in joy. With immeasurable skillful means he taught me the Dharma, arousing my aspiration and thirst, bringing me to accomplishment in joy. As is the method of all Buddhas, he first taught the proper Dharma that delights the listener: namely, teaching about generosity, teaching about morality, teaching about rebirth in the heavens; he censured desire as calamitous, birth and death as defilement; he praised desirelessness as sublime, and the factors of the path as pure and white. After the World-Honored One had taught me such Dharma, the Buddha knew that I had a joyful mind, a ready mind, a gentle mind, a receptive mind, a mind inclined upward, a single-pointed mind, a mind free of doubt, a mind free of hindrances, and that I had the ability and the power to receive the True Dharma. As all Buddhas teach the essential True Dharma, the World-Honored One then taught me about suffering, origin, cessation, and the path. At that time, right there on my seat, I saw the Four Noble Truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path. Just as a piece of clean white silk is easily dyed with color, venerable one, so too I, right there on my seat, saw the Four Noble Truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path. Venerable one, this is one quality I have."

The bhikṣu exclaimed: "Householder! If you have such a quality, how extraordinary! How remarkable!"

"Venerable one, I do not only have this quality. Furthermore, venerable one, having seen the Dharma, obtained the Dharma, realized the pure white Dharma, cut through doubt, crossed beyond perplexity, acknowledged no other teacher, no longer followed others, was without hesitation, had established myself in the fruit of realization, and had attained fearlessness in the World-Honored One's Dharma, venerable one, at that time I immediately rose from my seat, bowed my head at the Buddha's feet, and said: 'World-Honored One! I now take refuge in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha of bhikṣus. May the World-Honored One accept me as an upāsaka. From this day forth, I take refuge for life, until the end of my days. World-Honored One! From this day, I take from the World-Honored One the five precepts for the rest of my life, with the holy life as foremost.' Venerable one, since I took from the World-Honored One the five precepts for the rest of my life, with the holy life as foremost, I have never been aware of transgressing any precept. Venerable one, this is one quality I have."

The bhikṣu exclaimed: "Householder! If you have such a quality, how extraordinary! How remarkable!"

"Venerable one, I do not only have this quality. Furthermore, venerable one, at that time, after I had taken from the World-Honored One the five precepts for the rest of my life, with the holy life as foremost, I bowed my head at the Buddha's feet, circumambulated him three times, and departed. I returned to my home and gathered together all my wives. Having gathered them, I said: 'Do you know? I have taken from the World-Honored One the five precepts for the rest of my life, with the holy life as foremost. If any of you wish to remain here, you may remain here, practicing generosity and making merit. If you do not wish to remain, you may each return to your own families. If any of you wish to be given in marriage, I shall arrange your marriage.' Thereupon, my chief wife came and said to me: 'If you have taken from the Buddha the five precepts for the rest of your life, with the holy life as foremost, then please give me to such-and-such a man.' Venerable one, at that time I called for that man, and grasping my chief wife's arm with my left hand and holding a golden water vessel in my right hand, I said to that man: 'I now give you my chief wife to be your wife.' That man, upon hearing this, was greatly frightened, with hair standing on end all over his body, and said to me: 'Householder, do you wish to kill me? Householder, do you wish to kill me?' Venerable one, I said to him: 'I do not wish to kill you. However, I have taken from the Buddha the five precepts for the rest of my life, with the holy life as foremost. Therefore I give my chief wife to you to be your wife.' Venerable one, after I had given away my chief wife, whether during the giving, at the time of giving, or after the giving, I had no regret whatsoever in my mind. Venerable one, this is one quality I have."

The bhikṣu exclaimed: "Householder! If you have such a quality, how extraordinary! How remarkable!"

"Venerable one, I do not only have this quality. Furthermore, venerable one, when I go to the monastery grounds, if I first see a bhikṣu, I bow to him. If that bhikṣu is doing walking meditation, I also do walking meditation alongside him. If he is sitting, I also sit to one side. Having sat down, I listen to the Dharma. That venerable one teaches me the Dharma, and I also discuss the Dharma with that venerable one. That venerable one asks me about matters, and I also ask that venerable one about matters. That venerable one answers my questions, and I also answer that venerable one's questions. Venerable one, I have never been aware of showing disrespect to any senior, middle, or junior bhikṣu, or to any elder or senior bhikṣu. Venerable one, this is one quality I have."

The bhikṣu exclaimed: "Householder! If you have such a quality, how extraordinary! How remarkable!"

"Venerable one, I do not only have this quality. Furthermore, venerable one, when I am distributing gifts among the community of bhikṣus, a deva standing in the sky tells me: 'Householder! This one is an arhat. This one is on the path toward arhatship. This one is a non-returner. This one is on the path toward non-returning. This one is a once-returner. This one is on the path toward once-returning. This one is a stream-enterer. This one is on the path toward stream-entry. This one is diligent. This one is not diligent.' Venerable one, when I give to the community of bhikṣus, I have never been aware of having a discriminating mind. Venerable one, this is one quality I have."

The bhikṣu exclaimed: "Householder! If you have such a quality, how extraordinary! How remarkable!"

"Venerable one, I do not only have this quality. Furthermore, venerable one, when I am distributing gifts among the community of bhikṣus, a deva standing in the sky tells me: 'Householder! There is a Tathāgata, a Worthy One, a Perfectly Enlightened One. The World-Honored One has well taught the Dharma. The Tathāgata's noble assembly is well directed in practice.' Venerable one, I do not believe based on that deva's words, I do not take pleasure based on that deva, I do not follow what I have heard from that deva. Rather, I have my own pure knowledge, knowing that there is a Tathāgata, a Worthy One, a Perfectly Enlightened One, that the World-Honored One has well taught the Dharma, and that the Tathāgata's noble assembly is well directed in practice. Venerable one, this is one quality I have."

The bhikṣu exclaimed: "Householder! If you have such a quality, how extraordinary! How remarkable!"

"Venerable one, I do not only have this quality. Furthermore, venerable one, regarding the five lower fetters as taught by the Buddha: sensual desire, ill will, view of self, attachment to precepts and rituals, and doubt, I see that among these five, not one remains to bind me to return to this world and enter the womb. Venerable one, this is one quality I have."

The bhikṣu exclaimed: "Householder! If you have such a quality, how extraordinary! How remarkable!"

The householder Ugga said to the bhikṣu: "May the venerable one please take a meal here."

The bhikṣu, for the sake of the householder Ugga, silently accepted the invitation. The householder Ugga, knowing that the bhikṣu had silently accepted, immediately rose from his seat, personally brought water for hand-washing, and with the finest, most excellent, varied and abundant foods for eating, chewing, licking, and drinking, personally served and poured, ensuring that he was fully satisfied. After the meal was finished and the vessels were put away, and the water for hand-washing had been offered, he took a small seat and sat separately to listen to the Dharma. The bhikṣu taught the Dharma for the householder, arousing his aspiration and thirst, bringing him to accomplishment in joy. With immeasurable skillful means he taught him the Dharma, arousing his aspiration and thirst, bringing him to accomplishment in joy. Then he rose from his seat and departed, went to where the Buddha was, bowed his head at the Buddha's feet, sat to one side, and related to the Buddha in full everything that he and the householder Ugga had discussed.

Thereupon, the World-Honored One told the bhikṣus: "It is for this reason that I praised and commended the householder Ugga as possessing eight unprecedented qualities."

Thus spoke the Buddha. The bhikṣus, having heard what the Buddha said, rejoiced and practiced accordingly.

End of the Seventh Sūtra, the Sūtra of the Householder Ugga.

---

## (39) Sūtra of the Householder Ugga, Eighth of the Chapter on Unprecedented Qualities in the Madhyamāgama

Thus have I heard:

At one time, not long after the Buddha had entered parinirvāṇa, a number of senior elder bhikṣus were traveling in Vaiśālī, staying at the Monkey Pond Pavilion.

At that time, the householder Ugga had established such great offerings: namely, providing food for visitors from afar, providing food for travelers, the sick, and those who tend the sick, always providing gruel, always providing cooked rice, providing supplies for those who guard the monastery, always inviting a group of twenty to eat, and every five days inviting the entire community of bhikṣus to eat. He had established such great offerings. Furthermore, he had a merchant ship at sea, fully loaded with goods on its return voyage, worth a hundred thousand, which was entirely lost at one time. The many senior elder bhikṣus heard that the householder Ugga had established such great offerings: providing food for visitors from afar, providing food for travelers, the sick, and those who tend the sick, always providing gruel, always providing cooked rice, providing supplies for those who guard the monastery, always inviting a group of twenty to eat, and every five days inviting the entire community of bhikṣus to eat. Having heard this, they deliberated together: "Venerables! Who is able to go and tell the householder Ugga: 'Householder, you should stop! Do not continue making offerings. In time, householder, you will know for yourself'?" They then thought: "The Venerable Ānanda was the Buddha's attendant, received the World-Honored One's instruction, and was praised by the Buddha and by wise practitioners of the holy life. The Venerable Ānanda could go and tell the householder Ugga: 'Householder, you should stop! Do not continue making offerings. In time, householder, you will know for yourself.' Venerables! Let us together go to the Venerable Ānanda and speak of this matter."

Thereupon, the many senior elder bhikṣus went to where the Venerable Ānanda was, exchanged greetings with him, sat to one side, and said: "Venerable Ānanda, do you know? The householder Ugga has established such great offerings: providing food for visitors from afar, providing food for travelers, the sick, and those who tend the sick, always providing gruel, always providing cooked rice, providing supplies for those who guard the monastery, always inviting a group of twenty to eat, and every five days inviting the entire community of bhikṣus to eat. He has established such great offerings. Furthermore, he had a merchant ship at sea, fully loaded with goods on its return voyage, worth a hundred thousand, which was entirely lost at one time. We deliberated together, wondering who could go and tell the householder Ugga, saying: 'Householder, you should stop! Do not continue making offerings. In time, householder, you will know for yourself.' We then thought: 'The Venerable Ānanda was the Buddha's attendant, received the World-Honored One's instruction, and was praised by the Buddha and by wise practitioners of the holy life. The Venerable Ānanda could go and tell the householder Ugga: "Householder, you should stop! Do not continue making offerings. In time, householder, you will know for yourself."' Venerable Ānanda, please go to the householder Ugga and say to him: 'Householder, you should stop! Do not continue making offerings. In time, householder, you will know for yourself.'"

The Venerable Ānanda said to the senior elder bhikṣus: "Venerables! The householder Ugga is of a stern and upright nature. If I speak on my own behalf, he might become greatly displeased. Venerables! On whose behalf should I speak?"

The senior elder bhikṣus replied: "Venerable one! Speak on behalf of the community of bhikṣus. Having spoken on behalf of the community of bhikṣus, he will have nothing to say in objection." The Venerable Ānanda then silently accepted the commission of the senior elder bhikṣus. Thereupon, the senior elder bhikṣus, knowing that the Venerable Ānanda had silently accepted, rose from their seats, circumambulated the Venerable Ānanda, and each departed.

The next morning at dawn, the Venerable Ānanda donned his robes, took his bowl, and went to the home of the householder Ugga. The householder Ugga saw the Venerable Ānanda coming from afar, immediately rose from his seat, bared one shoulder, and with palms joined toward the Venerable Ānanda, said: "Welcome, Venerable Ānanda! It has been long since the Venerable Ānanda came here. Please be seated on this couch." The Venerable Ānanda then sat on the couch. The householder Ugga bowed at the Venerable Ānanda's feet and sat to one side.

The Venerable Ānanda said: "Householder, do you know? You have established such great offerings: providing food for visitors from afar, providing food for travelers, the sick, and those who tend the sick, always providing gruel, always providing cooked rice, providing supplies for those who guard the monastery, always inviting a group of twenty to eat, and every five days inviting the entire community of bhikṣus to eat. You have established such great offerings. Furthermore, you had a merchant ship at sea, fully loaded with goods on its return voyage, worth a hundred thousand, which was entirely lost at one time. Householder, you should stop! Do not continue making offerings. In time, householder, you will know for yourself."

The householder said: "Venerable Ānanda, whose words are these?"

The Venerable Ānanda replied: "Householder, I am conveying the words of the community of bhikṣus."

The householder said: "If the Venerable Ānanda conveys the words of the community of bhikṣus, there is nothing more to discuss. If these were your own words, they might cause great displeasure. Venerable Ānanda! Even if, through such giving and such generosity, all my wealth were completely exhausted, I only wish that my aspiration be fulfilled, like the aspiration of a wheel-turning king."

The Venerable Ānanda asked: "Householder, what is the aspiration of a wheel-turning king?"

The householder replied: "Venerable Ānanda! A poor person in a village thinks: 'May I become the wealthiest in the village!' That is his aspiration. The wealthiest person in a village thinks: 'May I become the wealthiest in the town!' That is his aspiration. The wealthiest person in a town thinks: 'May I become the wealthiest in the city!' That is his aspiration. The wealthiest person in a city thinks: 'May I become the chief magistrate of the city!' That is his aspiration. The chief magistrate of a city thinks: 'May I become the prime minister of the kingdom!' That is his aspiration. The prime minister thinks: 'May I become a minor king!' That is his aspiration. A minor king thinks: 'May I become a wheel-turning king!' That is his aspiration. A wheel-turning king thinks: 'May I be like a son of good family who shaves off his beard and hair, dons the kāṣāya robes, and with firm faith leaves the household life for the homeless life to train in the Way, namely, completing the supreme holy life; may I, in this present life, through my own knowledge and realization, directly witness and dwell in the attainment: Birth is ended, the holy life has been lived, what was to be done is done, there is no further becoming, knowing it as it truly is.' That is his aspiration. Venerable Ānanda! Even if, through such giving and such generosity, all my wealth were completely exhausted, I only wish that my aspiration be fulfilled, like the aspiration of a wheel-turning king. Venerable Ānanda, this is one quality I have."

The Venerable Ānanda exclaimed: "Householder! If you have such a quality, how extraordinary! How remarkable!"

"Furthermore, Venerable Ānanda, I do not only have this quality. Venerable Ānanda, when I go to the monastery grounds, if I first see a bhikṣu, I bow to him. If that bhikṣu is doing walking meditation, I also do walking meditation alongside him. If he is sitting, I also sit to one side. Having sat down, I listen to the Dharma. That venerable one teaches me the Dharma, and I also discuss the Dharma with that venerable one. That venerable one asks me about matters, and I also ask that venerable one about matters. That venerable one answers my questions, and I also answer that venerable one's questions. Venerable Ānanda, I have never been aware of showing disrespect to any senior, middle, or junior bhikṣu, or to any elder or senior bhikṣu. Venerable Ānanda, this is one quality I have."

The Venerable Ānanda exclaimed: "Householder! If you have such a quality, how extraordinary! How remarkable!"

"Furthermore, Venerable Ānanda, I do not only have this quality. Venerable Ānanda, when I am distributing gifts among the community of bhikṣus, a deva standing in the sky tells me: 'Householder! This one is an arhat. This one is on the path toward arhatship. This one is a non-returner. This one is on the path toward non-returning. This one is a once-returner. This one is on the path toward once-returning. This one is a stream-enterer. This one is on the path toward stream-entry. This one is diligent. This one is not diligent.' Venerable Ānanda, when I give to the community of bhikṣus, I have never been aware of having a discriminating mind. Venerable Ānanda, this is one quality I have."

The Venerable Ānanda exclaimed: "Householder! If you have such a quality, how extraordinary! How remarkable!"

"Furthermore, Venerable Ānanda, I do not only have this quality. Venerable Ānanda, when I am distributing gifts among the community of bhikṣus, a deva standing in the sky tells me: 'Householder! There is a Tathāgata, a Worthy One, a Perfectly Enlightened One. The World-Honored One has well taught the Dharma. The Tathāgata's noble assembly is well directed in practice.' I do not believe based on that deva's words, I do not take pleasure based on that deva, I do not follow what I have heard from that deva. Rather, I have my own pure knowledge, knowing that there is a Tathāgata, a Worthy One, a Perfectly Enlightened One, that the World-Honored One has well taught the Dharma, and that the Tathāgata's noble assembly is well directed in practice. Venerable Ānanda, this is one quality I have."

The Venerable Ānanda exclaimed: "Householder! If you have such a quality, how extraordinary! How remarkable!"

"Furthermore, Venerable Ānanda, I do not only have this quality. Venerable Ānanda, secluded from desires, secluded from unwholesome states, I have attained up to the fourth jhāna and dwell therein. Venerable Ānanda, this is one quality I have."

The Venerable Ānanda exclaimed: "Householder! If you have such a quality, how extraordinary! How remarkable!"

Thereupon, the householder Ugga said: "Venerable Ānanda, may you please take a meal here."

The Venerable Ānanda, for the sake of the householder Ugga, silently accepted the invitation. The householder Ugga, knowing that the Venerable Ānanda had silently accepted, immediately rose from his seat, personally brought water for hand-washing, and with the finest, most excellent, varied and abundant foods for eating, chewing, licking, and drinking, personally served and poured, ensuring that he was fully satisfied. After the meal was finished and the vessels were put away, and the water for hand-washing had been offered, he took a small seat and sat separately to listen to the Dharma. The Venerable Ānanda taught him the Dharma, arousing his aspiration and thirst, bringing him to accomplishment in joy. With immeasurable skillful means he taught him the Dharma, arousing his aspiration and thirst, bringing him to accomplishment in joy. Then he rose from his seat and departed.

The Venerable Ānanda spoke thus. The householder Ugga, having heard what the Venerable Ānanda said, rejoiced and practiced accordingly.

End of the Eighth Sūtra, the Sūtra of the Householder Ugga.

## (40) Sūtra of the Householder Hasta, Ninth of the Chapter on Unprecedented Qualities in the Madhyamāgama

Thus have I heard:

At one time, the Buddha was traveling in Āḷavī, in the Aggāḷava Forest.

At that time, the householder Hasta, together with five hundred great householders, went to where the Buddha was, bowed his head at the Buddha's feet, and sat to one side. The five hundred householders also bowed at the Buddha's feet and sat to one side.

The World-Honored One said: "Householder Hasta! You now have this extremely great assembly. Householder, by what methods do you gather this great assembly?"

At that time, the householder Hasta said: "World-Honored One! There are four methods of gathering, as taught by the World-Honored One: first, generosity; second, kind words; third, beneficial conduct; fourth, impartial cooperation. World-Honored One, I use these to gather the great assembly: sometimes through generosity, sometimes through kind words, sometimes through beneficial conduct, and sometimes through impartial cooperation."

The World-Honored One praised him: "Excellent! Excellent! Householder Hasta! You are able to gather the great assembly through proper methods, through proper means, and through proper causes and conditions. Householder Hasta, if in the past there were śramaṇas or brahmins who gathered great assemblies through proper methods, all of them used these four methods of gathering, or some among them. Householder Hasta, if in the future there will be śramaṇas or brahmins who gather great assemblies through proper methods, all of them will use these four methods of gathering, or some among them. Householder Hasta, if in the present there are śramaṇas or brahmins who gather great assemblies through proper methods, all of them use these four methods of gathering, or some among them."

Thereupon, the World-Honored One taught the Dharma for the householder Hasta, arousing his aspiration and thirst, bringing him to accomplishment in joy. With immeasurable skillful means he taught him the Dharma, arousing his aspiration and thirst, bringing him to accomplishment in joy. Then he sat in silence. Thereupon, after the Buddha had taught the householder Hasta the Dharma, arousing his aspiration and thirst, bringing him to accomplishment in joy, the householder rose from his seat, bowed to the Buddha, circumambulated him three times, and departed. He returned to his home. Upon reaching the outer gate, to all the people there he taught the Dharma, arousing their aspiration and thirst, bringing them to accomplishment in joy. At the middle gate, the inner gate, and upon entering inside, to all the people there he taught the Dharma, arousing their aspiration and thirst, bringing them to accomplishment in joy. Then he ascended the hall, spread out a seat, sat cross-legged, and with a mind imbued with loving-kindness, pervaded one direction and dwelt therein. Likewise the second, third, and fourth directions, the four intermediate directions, above and below, pervading everywhere universally: with a mind imbued with loving-kindness, without bonds, without enmity, without ill will, without contention, extremely vast and great, immeasurable and well cultivated, pervading the entire world, he dwelt therein. Likewise with compassion and sympathetic joy; with a mind imbued with equanimity, without bonds, without enmity, without ill will, without contention, extremely vast and great, immeasurable and well cultivated, pervading the entire world, he dwelt therein.

At that time, the Thirty-Three devas assembled in the Dharma hall and praised and commended the householder Hasta: "Venerables! The householder Hasta has gained great benefit and great merit. Why is this? The householder Hasta, after the Buddha had taught him the Dharma, arousing his aspiration and thirst, bringing him to accomplishment in joy, rose from his seat, bowed to the Buddha, circumambulated him three times, and departed. He returned to his home. Upon reaching the outer gate, to all the people there he taught the Dharma, arousing their aspiration and thirst, bringing them to accomplishment in joy. At the middle gate, the inner gate, and upon entering inside, to all the people there he taught the Dharma, arousing their aspiration and thirst, bringing them to accomplishment in joy. Then he ascended the hall, spread out a seat, sat cross-legged, and with a mind imbued with loving-kindness, pervaded one direction and dwelt therein. Likewise the second, third, and fourth directions, the four intermediate directions, above and below, pervading everywhere universally: with a mind imbued with loving-kindness, without bonds, without enmity, without ill will, without contention, extremely vast and great, immeasurable and well cultivated, pervading the entire world, he dwelt therein. Likewise with compassion and sympathetic joy; with a mind imbued with equanimity, without bonds, without enmity, without ill will, without contention, extremely vast and great, immeasurable and well cultivated, pervading the entire world, he dwelt therein."

Thereupon, the Great Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa, with a majestic and splendid appearance, brilliantly radiant, as the night was drawing toward dawn, went to the home of the householder Hasta and said: "Householder! You have gained great benefit and great merit. Why is this? Now the Thirty-Three devas have assembled for your sake in the Dharma hall, praising and commending you: 'The householder Hasta has gained great benefit and great merit. Why is this? Venerables! The householder Hasta, after the Buddha had taught him the Dharma, arousing his aspiration and thirst, bringing him to accomplishment in joy, rose from his seat, bowed to the Buddha, circumambulated him three times, and departed. He returned to his home. Upon reaching the outer gate, to all the people there he taught the Dharma, arousing their aspiration and thirst, bringing them to accomplishment in joy. At the middle gate, the inner gate, and upon entering inside, to all the people there he taught the Dharma, arousing their aspiration and thirst, bringing them to accomplishment in joy. Then he ascended the hall, spread out a seat, sat cross-legged, and with a mind imbued with loving-kindness, pervaded one direction and dwelt therein. Likewise the second, third, and fourth directions, the four intermediate directions, above and below, pervading everywhere universally: with a mind imbued with loving-kindness, without bonds, without enmity, without ill will, without contention, extremely vast and great, immeasurable and well cultivated, pervading the entire world, he dwelt therein. Likewise with compassion and sympathetic joy; with a mind imbued with equanimity, without bonds, without enmity, without ill will, without contention, extremely vast and great, immeasurable and well cultivated, pervading the entire world, he dwelt therein.'"

At that time, the householder Hasta remained silent without speaking, neither looking at nor gazing upon the Great Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa. Why was this? Because he held concentration in reverence and guarded his concentration.

At that time, the World-Honored One, amid countless hundreds of thousands in the assembly, praised and commended the householder Hasta: "The householder Hasta possesses seven unprecedented qualities. The householder Hasta, after I taught him the Dharma, arousing his aspiration and thirst, bringing him to accomplishment in joy, rose from his seat, bowed to me, circumambulated me three times, and departed. He returned to his home. Upon reaching the outer gate, to all the people there he taught the Dharma, arousing their aspiration and thirst, bringing them to accomplishment in joy. At the middle gate, the inner gate, and upon entering inside, to all the people there he taught the Dharma, arousing their aspiration and thirst, bringing them to accomplishment in joy. Then he ascended the hall, spread out a seat, sat cross-legged, and with a mind imbued with loving-kindness, pervaded one direction and dwelt therein. Likewise the second, third, and fourth directions, the four intermediate directions, above and below, pervading everywhere universally: with a mind imbued with loving-kindness, without bonds, without enmity, without ill will, without contention, extremely vast and great, immeasurable and well cultivated, pervading the entire world, he dwelt therein. Likewise with compassion and sympathetic joy; with a mind imbued with equanimity, without bonds, without enmity, without ill will, without contention, extremely vast and great, immeasurable and well cultivated, pervading the entire world, he dwelt therein.

"Now the Thirty-Three devas have assembled for him in the Dharma hall, praising and commending him: 'The householder Hasta has gained great benefit and great merit. Why is this? Venerables! The householder Hasta, after the Buddha had taught him the Dharma, arousing his aspiration and thirst, bringing him to accomplishment in joy, rose from his seat, bowed to the Buddha, circumambulated him three times, and departed. He returned to his home. Upon reaching the outer gate, to all the people there he taught the Dharma, arousing their aspiration and thirst, bringing them to accomplishment in joy. At the middle gate, the inner gate, and upon entering inside, to all the people there he taught the Dharma, arousing their aspiration and thirst, bringing them to accomplishment in joy. Likewise with compassion and sympathetic joy; with a mind imbued with equanimity, without bonds, without enmity, without ill will, without contention, extremely vast and great, immeasurable and well cultivated, pervading the entire world, he dwelt therein.'

"Now the Great Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa, with a majestic and splendid appearance, brilliantly radiant, as the night was drawing toward dawn, went to the home of the householder Hasta and said: 'Householder! You have gained great benefit and great merit. Why is this? Now the Thirty-Three devas have assembled for your sake in the Dharma hall, praising and commending you: "The householder Hasta has gained great benefit and great merit. Why is this? Venerables! The householder Hasta, after the Buddha had taught him the Dharma, arousing his aspiration and thirst, bringing him to accomplishment in joy, rose from his seat, bowed to the Buddha, circumambulated him three times, and departed. He returned to his home. Upon reaching the outer gate, to all the people there he taught the Dharma, arousing their aspiration and thirst, bringing them to accomplishment in joy. At the middle gate, the inner gate, and upon entering inside, to all the people there he taught the Dharma, arousing their aspiration and thirst, bringing them to accomplishment in joy. Then he ascended the hall, spread out a seat, sat cross-legged, and with a mind imbued with loving-kindness, pervaded one direction and dwelt therein. Likewise the second, third, and fourth directions, the four intermediate directions, above and below, pervading everywhere universally: with a mind imbued with loving-kindness, without bonds, without enmity, without ill will, without contention, extremely vast and great, immeasurable and well cultivated, pervading the entire world, he dwelt therein. Likewise with compassion and sympathetic joy; with a mind imbued with equanimity, without bonds, without enmity, without ill will, without contention, extremely vast and great, immeasurable and well cultivated, pervading the entire world, he dwelt therein."'"

Thereupon, a certain bhikṣu, the next morning at dawn, donned his robes, took his bowl, and went to the home of the householder Hasta. The householder Hasta saw the bhikṣu coming from afar, immediately rose from his seat, and with palms joined toward the bhikṣu, said: "Venerable one, welcome! It has been long since the venerable one came here. Please be seated on this couch." The bhikṣu then sat on the couch. The householder Hasta bowed at the bhikṣu's feet and sat to one side.

# Madhyamāgama (Middle Length Āgama) Fascicle 19
