---

*End of Fascicle 39 of the Madhyamāgama*

# Madhyamāgama, Fascicle 39

---

## (154) Sūtra on the Brahmin Vāseṭṭha Hall, Third in the Brahmin Chapter

Thus have I heard:

At one time, the Buddha was traveling in Śrāvastī, staying at the Eastern Park in the Hall of Migāra's Mother.

At that time, there were two persons, Vāseṭṭha and Bhāradvāja, of the brahmin clan, who had shaved off their hair and beards, put on kāṣāya robes, and with perfect faith had left the household life for homelessness to practice the Way. When the brahmins saw them, they severely reproached and reprimanded them, with great urgency and harshness, saying to them: "The brahmin caste is superior; all others are inferior. The brahmin caste is white; all others are black. Brahmins attain purity; non-brahmins do not attain purity. Brahmins are children of Brahmā, born from his mouth, created and transformed by Brahmā. You have abandoned what is superior to follow what is inferior, abandoned the white to follow the black. Those bald recluses are bound by darkness, cutting off the lineage, leaving no descendants. Therefore, what you have done is a great evil, an extreme transgression."

At that time, the World-Honored One, in the afternoon, rose from his seated meditation, came down from the hall, and in the open ground in the shadow of the hall walked back and forth in meditation, expounding the profound and subtle Dharma for the bhikṣus. The Venerable Vāseṭṭha saw from afar that the World-Honored One, in the afternoon, had risen from his seated meditation, come down from the hall, and in the open ground in the shadow of the hall was walking back and forth in meditation, expounding the profound and subtle Dharma for the bhikṣus. The Venerable Vāseṭṭha, seeing this, said: "Worthy Bhāradvāja! You should know that the World-Honored One, in the afternoon, has risen from his seated meditation, come down from the hall, and in the open ground in the shadow of the hall is walking back and forth in meditation, expounding the profound and subtle Dharma for the bhikṣus. Worthy Bhāradvāja! Let us go together to the Buddha; perhaps on this account we may hear the Dharma from the Buddha."

Thereupon, Vāseṭṭha and Bhāradvāja went to the Buddha, bowed their heads in salutation, and followed behind him as he walked in meditation.

The World-Honored One turned around and addressed those two: "Vāseṭṭha! You two brahmins have abandoned the brahmin clan, shaved off your hair and beards, put on kāṣāya robes, and with perfect faith have left the household life for homelessness to practice the Way. When the brahmins saw you, did they not severely reprimand you?"

They answered: "Indeed so, World-Honored One! When the brahmins saw us, they severely reproached and reprimanded us, with great urgency and harshness."

The World-Honored One asked: "Vāseṭṭha! When the brahmins saw you, how did they severely reproach and reprimand you, with great urgency and harshness?"

They answered: "World-Honored One! When the brahmins saw us, they said thus: 'The brahmin caste is superior; all others are inferior. The brahmin caste is white; all others are black. Brahmins attain purity; non-brahmins do not attain purity. Brahmins are children of Brahmā, born from his mouth, created and transformed by Brahmā. You have abandoned what is superior to follow what is inferior, abandoned the white to follow the black. Those bald recluses are bound by darkness, cutting off the lineage, leaving no descendants. Therefore, what you have done is a great evil, an extreme transgression.' World-Honored One! When the brahmins saw us, they thus severely reproached and reprimanded us, with great urgency and harshness."

The World-Honored One said: "Vāseṭṭha! What those brahmins said is most evil and utterly shameless. Why is that? Because those foolish ones, lacking skillful understanding and not recognizing the good field, are unable to know themselves, yet make such claims: 'We brahmins are children of Brahmā, born from his mouth, created and transformed by Brahmā.' Why is that? Vāseṭṭha! In this unsurpassed realization of knowledge and conduct, I do not speak of superiority by birth, do not speak of lineage, do not speak of pride, saying 'That one pleases me, that one displeases me,' based on seating, based on water, or based on the scriptures one has studied. Vāseṭṭha! If it were a matter of marriage, then one might speak of birth, speak of lineage, speak of pride, saying 'That one pleases me, that one displeases me,' based on seating, based on water, or based on the scriptures one has studied. Vāseṭṭha! If one reckons by birth, reckons by lineage, reckons by pride, such a person is extremely far removed from my unsurpassed realization of knowledge and conduct. Vāseṭṭha! Those who speak of birth, speak of lineage, speak of pride, saying 'That one pleases me, that one displeases me,' based on seating, based on water, or based on the scriptures one has studied, are separated from my unsurpassed realization of knowledge and conduct.

"Furthermore, Vāseṭṭha! There are three classes regarding which not everyone disputes together, yet which involve a mixture of wholesome and unwholesome dharmas; they are praised or not praised by the Noble Ones. What are the three? The kṣatriya class, the brahmin class, and the householder class. Vāseṭṭha! What do you think? Can a kṣatriya kill living beings, take what is not given, engage in sexual misconduct, speak falsely, and even hold wrong views? And can a householder do the same? Is it not so for brahmins as well?"

He answered: "World-Honored One! A kṣatriya can also kill living beings, take what is not given, engage in sexual misconduct, speak falsely, and even hold wrong views. Brahmins and householders are likewise."

The World-Honored One asked: "Vāseṭṭha! What do you think? Can a brahmin abstain from killing, cease killing, cease taking what is not given, cease sexual misconduct, cease false speech, and even abandon wrong views to attain right views? Can kṣatriyas and householders not do the same?"

He answered: "World-Honored One! A brahmin can also abstain from killing, cease killing, cease taking what is not given, cease sexual misconduct, cease false speech, and even abandon wrong views to attain right views. Kṣatriyas and householders are likewise."

The World-Honored One asked: "Vāseṭṭha! What do you think? If there are immeasurable evil, unwholesome dharmas, are they practiced only by kṣatriyas and householders, and not by brahmins? If there are immeasurable wholesome dharmas, are they practiced only by brahmins, and not by kṣatriyas and householders?"

He answered: "World-Honored One! If there are immeasurable evil, unwholesome dharmas, kṣatriyas and householders can practice them, and brahmins likewise. If there are immeasurable wholesome dharmas, brahmins can practice them, and kṣatriyas and householders likewise."

"Vāseṭṭha! If immeasurable evil, unwholesome dharmas were exclusively practiced by kṣatriyas and householders and not by brahmins, and if immeasurable wholesome dharmas were exclusively practiced by brahmins and not by kṣatriyas and householders, then those brahmins could make such a claim: 'We brahmins are children of Brahmā, born from his mouth, created and transformed by Brahmā.' Why is that? Vāseṭṭha! One sees brahmin women at the time of their first marriage, after marriage one sees them with bodies bearing pregnancy, after pregnancy one sees them giving birth, to either boys or girls. Vāseṭṭha! Thus brahmins also follow worldly ways and are born through the birth canal. Yet they falsely speak and slander Brahmā, making such claims: 'We brahmins are children of Brahmā, born from his mouth, created and transformed by Brahmā.'

"Vāseṭṭha! If sons of good families of various clans and various names, abandoning various clans, shave off their hair and beards, put on kāṣāya robes, and with perfect faith leave the household life for homelessness to practice the Way under me, they should make such a claim: 'We brahmins are children of Brahmā, born from his mouth, created and transformed by Brahmā.' Why is that? Vāseṭṭha! Those sons of good families who enter my True Dharma and Vinaya, who receive my True Dharma and Vinaya, attain the other shore, cut off doubt, transcend perplexity, are without hesitation, and in the World-Honored One's Dharma attain fearlessness. Therefore, they should make such a claim: 'We brahmins are children of Brahmā, born from his mouth, created and transformed by Brahmā.' Vāseṭṭha! That Brahmā is a designation for the Tathāgata, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Enlightened One. Brahmā is the Tathāgata. Coolness is the Tathāgata. Without affliction, without fever, not departing from suchness: this is the Tathāgata. Vāseṭṭha! What do you think? Do the Śākya clansmen humbly love, revere, deeply respect, make offerings to, and attend upon King Prasenajit of Kosala?"

He then answered: "So it is, World-Honored One."

The World-Honored One asked: "Vāseṭṭha! What do you think? If the Śākya clansmen humbly love, revere, deeply respect, make offerings to, and attend upon King Prasenajit of Kosala, does King Prasenajit of Kosala likewise humbly love, revere, deeply respect, make offerings to, and attend upon me?"

He answered the World-Honored One: "That the Śākya clansmen humbly love, revere, deeply respect, make offerings to, and attend upon King Prasenajit of Kosala is nothing remarkable. But that King Prasenajit of Kosala humbly loves, reveres, deeply respects, makes offerings to, and attends upon the World-Honored One is truly remarkable."

The World-Honored One said: "Vāseṭṭha! King Prasenajit of Kosala does not have such thoughts when he humbly loves, reveres, deeply respects, makes offerings to, and attends upon me, thinking: 'The recluse Gautama's clan is extremely high while my clan is low. The recluse Gautama has abundant wealth while I have little wealth. The recluse Gautama's form and appearance are supremely wonderful while my appearance is not wonderful. The recluse Gautama has great spiritual power while I have little spiritual power. The recluse Gautama has excellent wisdom while I have poor wisdom.' Vāseṭṭha! Rather, King Prasenajit of Kosala loves and reveres the Dharma, deeply respects it, and makes offerings for the sake of attending upon it, and thus he humbly loves, reveres, deeply respects, makes offerings to, and attends upon me."

At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the bhikṣus: "Vāseṭṭha! There is a time when this world entirely disintegrates. When this world disintegrates, if there are beings who are reborn in the Ābhāsvara Heaven, they dwell there with subtle forms, mind-made, with all limbs and faculties complete, feeding on joy, with light from their own bodies, traversing space, dwelling in a pure state for a long time.

"Vāseṭṭha! There is a time when this great earth is filled entirely with water. Above that great water, the wind blows and churns, forming an essence through construction and gathering, combining and aggregating, just as when one churns ripened curds by stirring the milk, forming an essence through construction and gathering, combining and aggregating. In this way, Vāseṭṭha, there is a time when this great earth is filled entirely with water. Above that great water, the wind blows and churns, forming an essence through construction and gathering, combining and aggregating. From this, earth-savory is produced, having color, fragrance, and flavor. What is its color? It is like the color of fresh ghee and clarified ghee. What is its flavor? It is like the flavor of honey-balls.

"Vāseṭṭha! There is a time when this world re-forms again. If there are beings who had been reborn in the Ābhāsvara Heaven, whose lifespan is exhausted, whose karma is exhausted, whose merit is exhausted, who die and are reborn here as humans, after being reborn here, they have subtle forms, mind-made, with all limbs and faculties complete, feeding on joy, with light from their own bodies, traversing space, dwelling in a pure state for a long time. Vāseṭṭha! At that time, in the world there is no sun or moon, nor are there stars and constellations, no day or night, no month or half-month, no seasons or years. Vāseṭṭha! At that time, there are no fathers, no mothers, no males, no females, no masters, no servants; there are only equal beings.

"Then, one being, greedy and not restrained, thought: 'What is this earth-savory? I should scoop up some of this earth-savory with my finger and taste it.' At that time, the being scooped up the earth-savory with his finger and tasted it. Thus, the beings, having come to know the earth-savory, desired to eat more of it. At that time, a being thought: 'Why should I eat this earth-savory with my finger, tiring myself? I should rather scoop up this earth-savory with my hands and eat it.' At that time, the being scooped up the earth-savory with his hands and ate it. Among those beings, there was another being who saw the others each scooping up the earth-savory with their hands and eating it, and thought: 'This is truly excellent, this is truly delightful. I too should scoop up this earth-savory with my hands and eat it.' At that time, the being scooped up the earth-savory with his hands and ate it.

"When those beings scooped up the earth-savory with their hands and ate it, in this way and that way, their bodies grew increasingly thick, increasingly heavy, and increasingly coarse. The pure appearance that they had previously possessed then vanished, and natural darkness arose. Vāseṭṭha! It is a worldly principle that this naturally occurs. When darkness arises, the sun and moon must arise. When the sun and moon arise, stars and constellations arise. When stars and constellations arise, day and night are established. When day and night are established, months and half-months come to be, and seasons and years come to be. Those beings ate the earth-savory and dwelt in the world for a long time.

"Vāseṭṭha! Among those beings, those who ate much of the earth-savory developed a coarse appearance, while those who ate little of it retained a refined appearance. From this, it became known that appearances were either superior or inferior. Because of the superiority or inferiority of appearance, beings looked down upon one another, saying: 'My appearance is superior; your appearance is inferior.' Because of the pride and unwholesome dharmas arising from superiority and inferiority of appearance, the earth-savory vanished. When the earth-savory vanished, those beings gathered together, wept bitterly, and said: 'Alas for the earth-savory! Alas for the earth-savory!' Just as people today, when savoring a delicious thing, do not speak its original name; although they retain the expression, they do not know its meaning. Explaining this by examining the meaning is likewise. Vāseṭṭha! After the earth-savory vanished, those beings produced earth-fat, which had color, fragrance, and flavor. What was its color? It was like the color of fresh ghee and clarified ghee. What was its flavor? It was like the flavor of honey-balls. They ate this earth-fat and dwelt in the world for a long time.

"Vāseṭṭha! Among those beings, those who ate much of the earth-fat developed a coarse appearance, while those who ate little of it retained a refined appearance. From this, it became known that appearances were either superior or inferior. Because of the superiority or inferiority of appearance, beings looked down upon one another, saying: 'My appearance is superior; your appearance is inferior.' Because of the pride and unwholesome dharmas arising from superiority and inferiority of appearance, the earth-fat vanished. When the earth-fat vanished, those beings gathered together, wept bitterly, and said: 'Alas for the earth-fat! Alas for the earth-fat!' Just as people today, when chastised by others, do not speak the original name; although they retain the expression, they do not know its meaning. Explaining this by examining the meaning is likewise.

"Vāseṭṭha! After the earth-fat vanished, those beings produced a creeping plant called vāḷa, which had color, fragrance, and flavor. What was its color? It was like the color of the udumbara flower. What was its flavor? It was like the flavor of fine honey-balls. They ate this vāḷa and dwelt in the world for a long time.

"Vāseṭṭha! Among those beings, those who ate much of the vāḷa developed a coarse appearance, while those who ate little of it retained a refined appearance. From this, it became known that appearances were either superior or inferior. Because of the superiority or inferiority of appearance, beings looked down upon one another, saying: 'My appearance is superior; your appearance is inferior.' Because of the pride and unwholesome dharmas arising from superiority and inferiority of appearance, the vāḷa vanished. When the vāḷa vanished, those beings gathered together, wept bitterly, and said: 'Alas for the vāḷa! Alas for the vāḷa!' Just as people today, when touched by suffering, do not speak the original name; although they retain the expression, they do not know its meaning. Explaining this by examining the meaning is likewise.

"Vāseṭṭha! After the vāḷa vanished, those beings produced a naturally growing rice, white and pure, without husks, also without chaff or stalks, four inches long. When cut in the morning, it grew back by evening; when cut in the evening, it grew back by morning. When cooked, it had a salty flavor and was without any raw taste. The beings ate this naturally growing rice. After those beings ate this naturally growing rice, various physical forms arose among them. Some beings developed male forms, and some beings developed female forms. When those beings developed male and female forms, upon seeing each other, they said: 'An evil being has arisen! An evil being has arisen!'

"Vāseṭṭha! 'An evil being has arisen' refers to speaking of women. When those beings developed male and female forms, those beings then watched one another. After watching one another, their eyes met in gazing. After gazing at one another, they became attracted to one another. After becoming attracted to one another, they experienced feverish desire. After experiencing feverish desire, they became attached to one another. After becoming attached to one another, they engaged in sexual intercourse. When others saw them engaging in sexual intercourse, they threw sticks, stones, staffs, and clods at them, saying: 'Bah! Wicked beings, doing unlawful things! How can beings do such things together?' Just as people today, when welcoming a new bride, scatter wrapped flowers or hang flower garlands, saying: 'May the bride have peace! May the bride have peace!' What was formerly despised is now loved.

"Vāseṭṭha! If there were beings who felt shame and disgust toward evil, impure dharmas, who were embarrassed and ashamed, they would leave the group for one day, two days, up to six or seven days, half a month, one month, or even a year. Vāseṭṭha! If there were beings who wished to engage in this impure conduct, they would build houses and say: 'We do evil within, we do evil within.' Vāseṭṭha! This is the first cause and first condition for the arising of the institution of houses in the world, an ancient and foremost wisdom, in accordance with Dharma, not contrary to Dharma, a standard honored by people of Dharma.

"Among them, there was one lazy being who thought: 'Why do I take naturally growing rice day after day? I should rather gather rice for one day's food all at once.' He then gathered rice for one day's food all at once. Then, another being said to that being: 'Being! Will you come along to gather rice?' That one answered: 'I have already gathered all at once. Go gather yours yourself.' That being, hearing this, thought: 'This is truly excellent, this is truly delightful. I too should gather tomorrow's rice all at once.' He then gathered the next day's rice as well.

"Again, another being said to that being: 'Being! Will you come along to gather rice?' That one answered: 'I have already gathered tomorrow's rice as well. Go gather yours yourself.' That being, hearing this, thought: 'This is truly excellent, this is truly delightful. I should now gather rice for seven days all at once.' At that time, that being then gathered rice for seven days all at once. As those beings excessively gathered and stored the naturally growing rice, the stored rice developed husks and chaff. When cut, even up to seven days later it also developed husks and chaff. Wherever it was cut, it no longer grew back.

"Then, those beings gathered together, wept bitterly, and said these words: 'We have given rise to evil, unwholesome dharmas through our storing and accumulating of rice. Why is that? We originally had subtle forms, mind-made, with all limbs and faculties complete, feeding on joy, with light from our own bodies, traversing space, dwelling in a pure state for a long time. We produced the earth-savory, which had color, fragrance, and flavor. What was its color? It was like the color of fresh ghee and clarified ghee. What was its flavor? It was like the flavor of honey-balls. We ate the earth-savory and dwelt in the world for a long time. Among us, those who ate much of the earth-savory developed a coarse appearance, while those who ate little of it retained a refined appearance. From this, it became known that appearances were either superior or inferior. Because of the superiority or inferiority of appearance, we looked down upon one another, saying: "My appearance is superior; your appearance is inferior." Because of the pride and unwholesome dharmas arising from superiority and inferiority of appearance, the earth-savory vanished. After the earth-savory vanished, we produced earth-fat, which had color, fragrance, and flavor. What was its color? It was like the color of fresh ghee and clarified ghee. What was its flavor? It was like the flavor of honey-balls. We ate the earth-fat and dwelt in the world for a long time. Among us, those who ate much of the earth-fat developed a coarse appearance, while those who ate little of it retained a refined appearance. From this, it became known that appearances were either superior or inferior. Because of the superiority or inferiority of appearance, we looked down upon one another, saying: "My appearance is superior; your appearance is inferior." Because of the pride and unwholesome dharmas arising from superiority and inferiority of appearance, the earth-fat vanished. After the earth-fat vanished, we produced vāḷa, which had color, fragrance, and flavor. What was its color? It was like the color of the udumbara flower. What was its flavor? It was like the flavor of fine honey-balls. We ate the vāḷa and dwelt in the world for a long time. Among us, those who ate much of the vāḷa developed a coarse appearance, while those who ate little of it retained a refined appearance. From this, it became known that appearances were either superior or inferior. Because of the superiority or inferiority of appearance, we looked down upon one another, saying: "My appearance is superior; your appearance is inferior." Because of the pride and unwholesome dharmas arising from superiority and inferiority of appearance, the vāḷa vanished. After the vāḷa vanished, we produced naturally growing rice, white and pure, without husks, also without chaff or stalks, four inches long. When cut in the morning, it grew back by evening; when cut in the evening, it grew back by morning. When cooked, it had a salty flavor and was without any raw taste. We ate this naturally growing rice. Yet because we excessively gathered and stored the naturally growing rice, the stored rice developed husks and chaff. When cut up to seven days later, it also developed husks and chaff. Wherever it was cut, it no longer grew back. We should now create cultivated fields, set up boundary markers!'

"Thereupon, those beings created cultivated fields and set up boundary markers. Among them, one being who had his own rice crop entered another's field and stole another's rice. The owner saw this and said: 'Bah! Bah! Wicked being, why do you do this? You have your own rice, yet you enter another's field and steal another's rice. You may go now, but do not do this again.' Yet that being again, a second and third time, stole another's rice. The owner also, a second and third time, saw this, and then punched and grabbed him and dragged him before the assembly, saying to the assembly: 'This being has his own rice crop, yet he enters my field and steals my rice.' And that being also said to the assembly: 'This being punched and grabbed me and dragged me here before the assembly.'

"Then, those many beings gathered together in assembly, wept bitterly, and said these words: 'We have given rise to evil, unwholesome dharmas, namely the guarding of fields. Why is that? Because of guarding fields, there arise disputes, losses, exhaustion, accusations of one another, punching and grabbing one another. We should now, from among our assembly, select one who is most handsome in form and appearance, supremely wonderful and foremost, and establish him as field-lord. Whomever should be reproved, he shall reprove. Whomever should be expelled, he shall expel. And from the rice that we obtain, we shall lawfully contribute a share and send it to him.' Thereupon, among those beings, the one who was most handsome in form and appearance, supremely wonderful and foremost, was selected by the assembly and established as field-lord. Whomever should be reproved, he reproved. Whomever should be expelled, he expelled. And when there was rice, it was lawfully contributed and sent to him as field-lord.

"This field-lord is called 'kṣatriya.' One who makes beings happy according to Dharma, who guards and practices the precepts, is a king. This king is called 'king.' Vāseṭṭha! This is the first cause and first condition for the arising of the kṣatriya class in the world, an ancient and foremost wisdom, in accordance with Dharma, not contrary to Dharma, a standard honored by people of Dharma.

"Then, certain other beings regarded guarding as a sickness, regarded guarding as a boil, regarded guarding as an arrow-thorn, and so they abandoned guarding and retreated to secluded places, built huts of grass and leaves, and practiced meditation. Those beings, returning from their solitary retreats, each morning at dawn entered villages, towns, and royal cities to beg for food. The many beings, seeing them, offered them gifts, revered and honored them, saying: 'These are different beings who regard guarding as a sickness, regard guarding as a boil, regard guarding as an arrow-thorn, and so they have abandoned guarding and retreated to secluded places, built huts of grass and leaves, and practice meditation. These venerable ones have cast off harmful, evil, unwholesome dharmas; they are brahmins.' These brahmins are called 'brahmins.'

"Those beings, practicing meditation, could not attain meditation; practicing austerities, could not attain the fruit of austerities; practicing seclusion, could not attain the fruit of seclusion; practicing one-pointedness of mind, could not attain one-pointedness of mind; practicing vigor, could not attain the fruit of vigor. So they abandoned the wilderness and returned to villages, towns, and royal cities, built four-pillared houses, and composed and established scriptures. The many beings, seeing this, no longer offered them gifts, no longer revered and honored them, and said: 'These are different beings who formerly regarded guarding as a sickness, regarded guarding as a boil, regarded guarding as an arrow-thorn, and so they had abandoned guarding and retreated to secluded places, built huts of grass and leaves, and practiced meditation, yet they could not attain meditation; they practiced austerities but could not attain the fruit of austerities; they practiced seclusion but could not attain the fruit of seclusion; they practiced one-pointedness of mind but could not attain one-pointedness of mind; they practiced vigor but could not attain the fruit of vigor. So they abandoned the wilderness and returned to villages, towns, and royal cities, built four-pillared houses, and composed and established scriptures. These venerable ones have now pursued learning and are no longer practicing meditation; they are learned ones.' These learned ones are called 'learned ones.' Vāseṭṭha! This is the first cause and first condition for the arising of the brahmin class in the world, an ancient and foremost wisdom, in accordance with Dharma, not contrary to Dharma, a standard honored by people of Dharma.

"Then, certain other beings went to various regions and took up farming. These went to various regions and took up farming. These went to various regions and took up farming; they are called 'vaiśyas.' Vāseṭṭha! This is the first cause and first condition for the arising of the vaiśya class in the world, an ancient and foremost wisdom, in accordance with Dharma, not contrary to Dharma, a standard honored by people of Dharma.

"Vāseṭṭha! After these three classes had arisen in the world, it then became known that there was a fourth class, that of recluses. How is it that after these three classes had arisen in the world, it became known that there was a fourth class of recluses? From among the kṣatriya clan, sons of the clan were able to reproach themselves for evil, unwholesome dharmas, to feel disgust and loathing for evil, unwholesome dharmas, and they shaved off their hair and beards, put on kāṣāya robes, and with perfect faith left the household life for homelessness to practice the Way, thinking: 'I shall become a recluse and practice the holy life.' And so they became recluses and practiced the holy life. Likewise, sons of the brahmin clan and sons of the vaiśya clan also reproached themselves for evil, unwholesome dharmas, felt disgust and loathing for evil, unwholesome dharmas, shaved off their hair and beards, put on kāṣāya robes, and with perfect faith left the household life for homelessness to practice the Way, also thinking: 'I shall become a recluse and practice the holy life.' And so they became recluses and practiced the holy life. Vāseṭṭha! Thus, after these three classes had arisen in the world, it became known that there was a fourth class of recluses.

"Vāseṭṭha! I shall now explain in detail these three classes. How are these three classes explained in detail? Sons of the kṣatriya clan who practice unwholesome dharmas with body, who practice unwholesome dharmas with speech and mind, when their bodies break up and their lives end, will one-sidedly experience suffering. Likewise, sons of the brahmin clan and sons of the vaiśya clan who practice unwholesome dharmas with body, who practice unwholesome dharmas with speech and mind, when their bodies break up and their lives end, will one-sidedly experience suffering.

"Vāseṭṭha! Sons of the kṣatriya clan who practice wholesome dharmas with body, who practice wholesome dharmas with speech and mind, when their bodies break up and their lives end, will one-sidedly experience happiness. Likewise, sons of the brahmin clan and sons of the vaiśya clan who practice wholesome dharmas with body, who practice wholesome dharmas with speech and mind, when their bodies break up and their lives end, will one-sidedly experience happiness.

"Vāseṭṭha! Sons of the kṣatriya clan who practice mixed conduct with body, along with guarded conduct, who practice mixed conduct with speech and mind, along with guarded conduct, when their bodies break up and their lives end, will experience both suffering and happiness. Likewise, sons of the brahmin clan and sons of the vaiśya clan who practice mixed conduct with body, along with guarded conduct, who practice mixed conduct with speech and mind, along with guarded conduct, when their bodies break up and their lives end, will experience both suffering and happiness.

"Vāseṭṭha! Sons of the kṣatriya clan who cultivate the seven factors of awakening, with skillful thought and skillful contemplation, who know thus and see thus, whose minds are liberated from the outflow of desire, whose minds are liberated from the outflow of existence and from the outflow of ignorance, being liberated, they know they are liberated: 'Birth is ended, the holy life has been established, what was to be done has been done, there will be no more receiving of any state of being,' and they know it as it truly is. Likewise, sons of the brahmin clan and sons of the vaiśya clan who cultivate the seven factors of awakening, with skillful thought and skillful contemplation, who know thus and see thus, whose minds are liberated from the outflow of desire, whose minds are liberated from the outflow of existence and from the outflow of ignorance, being liberated, they know they are liberated: 'Birth is ended, the holy life has been established, what was to be done has been done, there will be no more receiving of any state of being,' and they know it as it truly is. Vāseṭṭha! Such is the detailed explanation of these three classes. The Lord of Brahmā spoke this verse:

"'The kṣatriya is honored among bipeds,
For having clan and lineage;
But one who seeks knowledge and conduct,
That one is praised by gods and humans.'

"Vāseṭṭha! The Lord of Brahmā skillfully spoke this verse; it was not unskillfully spoken. It was skillfully chanted and recited; it was not unskillfully done. It was skillfully expressed in words; it was not unskillfully done. The meaning of what was said is thus:

"'The kṣatriya is honored among bipeds,
For having clan and lineage;
But one who seeks knowledge and conduct,
That one is praised by gods and humans.'

"Why is that? I also say the same:

"'The kṣatriya is honored among bipeds,
For having clan and lineage;
But one who seeks knowledge and conduct,
That one is praised by gods and humans.'"

Thus spoke the Buddha. The Venerable Vāseṭṭha, Bhāradvāja, and the bhikṣus, hearing what the Buddha had said, rejoiced and practiced accordingly.

## (155) Sūtra on Sudatta, Fourth in the Brahmin Chapter

Thus have I heard:

At one time, the Buddha was traveling in Śrāvastī, staying in the Jeta Grove in Anāthapiṇḍada's Park.

At that time, the householder Sudatta went to the Buddha, bowed his head in salutation, and sat to one side.

The World-Honored One asked: "Householder, does your household practice giving?"

The householder Sudatta answered: "Indeed so, World-Honored One. Our household practices giving, but it is very coarse and cannot be fine. We give rice mixed with bran, soup of hemp, and a piece of ginger and vegetables."

The World-Honored One said: "Householder! Whether one gives coarse food or fine food, both receive their reward. Householder! If one practices coarse giving but gives without faith, gives without deliberate intention, does not give with one's own hands, does not go personally to give, gives without reflection, gives not on the basis of faith, and gives without contemplating the fruit of karma, then one should observe the resulting reward: the mind will not desire a good household, will not desire fine vehicles, will not desire fine clothing and bedding, will not desire fine food and drink, will not desire fine enjoyment of the five sense-pleasures. Why is that? Because the giving was not done wholeheartedly. Householder! You should know that the resulting reward is like this.

"Householder! If one practices coarse giving but gives with faith, gives with deliberate intention, gives with one's own hands, goes personally to give, gives with reflection, gives on the basis of faith, and gives while contemplating the fruit of karma, then one should observe the resulting reward: the mind will desire a good household, will desire fine vehicles, will desire fine clothing and bedding, will desire fine food and drink, will desire fine enjoyment of the five sense-pleasures. Why is that? Because the giving was done wholeheartedly. Householder! You should know that the resulting reward is like this.

"Householder! If one practices fine giving but gives without faith, gives without deliberate intention, does not give with one's own hands, does not go personally to give, gives without reflection, gives not on the basis of faith, and gives without contemplating the fruit of karma, then one should observe the resulting reward: the mind will not desire a good household, will not desire fine vehicles, will not desire fine clothing and bedding, will not desire fine food and drink, will not desire fine enjoyment of the five sense-pleasures. Why is that? Because the giving was not done wholeheartedly. Householder! You should know that the resulting reward is like this.

"Householder! If one practices fine giving and gives with faith, gives with deliberate intention, gives with one's own hands, goes personally to give, gives with reflection, gives on the basis of faith, and gives while contemplating the fruit of karma, then one should observe the resulting reward: the mind will desire a good household, will desire fine vehicles, will desire fine clothing and bedding, will desire fine food and drink, will desire fine enjoyment of the five sense-pleasures. Why is that? Because the giving was done wholeheartedly. Householder! You should know that the resulting reward is like this.

"Householder! In the past, long ago, there was a brahmin great elder named Velāma, who was extremely wealthy, prosperous, with immeasurable resources, fiefs, and towns yielding revenue, and many precious treasures, with livestock and property beyond reckoning. He practiced giving in this manner: eighty-four thousand golden bowls filled with crushed silver; such was his great giving. Eighty-four thousand silver bowls filled with crushed gold; such was his great giving. Eighty-four thousand golden bowls filled with crushed gold; such was his great giving. Eighty-four thousand silver bowls filled with crushed silver; such was his great giving. Eighty-four thousand elephants, adorned and decorated, with white coverings placed over them; such was his great giving. Eighty-four thousand horses, adorned and decorated, with white coverings and golden ornamental trappings; such was his great giving. Eighty-four thousand cows, with cloth ropes and cloth coverings, each yielding one measure of milk; such was his great giving. Eighty-four thousand maidens, of beautiful and elegant appearance, delightful to behold, adorned with all manner of precious jeweled ornaments; such was his great giving. How much more the other food, provisions, and delicacies!

"Householder! If the brahmin Velāma practiced such great giving, and if furthermore one were to give food filling the entire Jambudvīpa to ordinary people, this latter giving would be more excellent than the former. Householder! If the brahmin Velāma practiced such great giving, and also gave food filling the entire Jambudvīpa to ordinary people, and if furthermore one were to give food to a single stream-enterer, this latter giving would be the most excellent. Householder! If the brahmin Velāma practiced such great giving, and also gave food filling the entire Jambudvīpa to ordinary people, and gave food to a hundred stream-enterers, and if furthermore one were to give food to a single once-returner, this latter giving would be the most excellent. Householder! If the brahmin Velāma practiced such great giving, and also gave food filling the entire Jambudvīpa to ordinary people, and gave food to a hundred stream-enterers and a hundred once-returners, and if furthermore one were to give food to a single non-returner, this latter giving would be the most excellent. Householder! If the brahmin Velāma practiced such great giving, and also gave food filling the entire Jambudvīpa to ordinary people, and gave food to a hundred stream-enterers, a hundred once-returners, and a hundred non-returners, and if furthermore one were to give food to a single arhat, this latter giving would be the most excellent.

"Householder! If the brahmin Velāma practiced such great giving, and also gave food filling the entire Jambudvīpa to ordinary people, and gave food to a hundred stream-enterers, a hundred once-returners, a hundred non-returners, and a hundred arhats, and if furthermore one were to give food to a single pratyekabuddha, this latter giving would be the most excellent. Householder! If the brahmin Velāma practiced such great giving, and also gave food filling the entire Jambudvīpa to ordinary people, and gave food to a hundred stream-enterers, a hundred once-returners, a hundred non-returners, a hundred arhats, and a hundred pratyekabuddhas, and if furthermore one were to give food to a single Tathāgata, Worthy One, Perfectly Enlightened One, this latter giving would be the most excellent. Householder! If the brahmin Velāma practiced such great giving, and also gave food filling the entire Jambudvīpa to ordinary people, and gave food to a hundred stream-enterers, a hundred once-returners, a hundred non-returners, a hundred arhats, and a hundred pratyekabuddhas, and if furthermore one were to build a dwelling and offer it to the Sangha of the four directions, this latter giving would be the most excellent.

"Householder! If the brahmin Velāma practiced such great giving, and also gave food filling the entire Jambudvīpa to ordinary people, and gave food to a hundred stream-enterers, a hundred once-returners, a hundred non-returners, a hundred arhats, and a hundred pratyekabuddhas, and built a dwelling and offered it to the Sangha of the four directions, and if furthermore one were to take refuge with a joyful heart in the Three Treasures, the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha of bhikṣus, and also undertake the precepts, this latter giving would be the most excellent. Householder! If the brahmin Velāma practiced such great giving, and also gave food filling the entire Jambudvīpa to ordinary people, and gave food to a hundred stream-enterers, a hundred once-returners, a hundred non-returners, a hundred arhats, and a hundred pratyekabuddhas, and built a dwelling and offered it to the Sangha of the four directions, and with a joyful heart took refuge in the Three Treasures, the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha of bhikṣus, and also undertook the precepts, and if furthermore one were to practice loving-kindness toward all living beings, even for the time it takes to milk a cow, this latter would be the most excellent.

"Householder! If the brahmin Velāma practiced such great giving, and also gave food filling the entire Jambudvīpa to ordinary people, and gave food to a hundred stream-enterers, a hundred once-returners, a hundred non-returners, a hundred arhats, and a hundred pratyekabuddhas, and built a dwelling and offered it to the Sangha of the four directions, and with a joyful heart took refuge in the Three Treasures, the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha of bhikṣus, and also undertook the precepts, and practiced loving-kindness toward all living beings, even for the time it takes to milk a cow, and if furthermore one were to contemplate that all dharmas are impermanent, suffering, empty, and without self, this latter would be the most excellent.

"What do you think, householder? The brahmin great elder of that past time named Velāma, do you think he was someone else? Do not think so. Why is that? You should know that he was none other than myself. In the past, I was the brahmin great elder named Velāma. Householder! At that time, I benefited myself and also benefited others, benefited many people, had compassion for the world, and for the sake of gods and humans sought meaning, benefit, peace, and happiness. At that time, the Dharma I taught did not reach the ultimate, did not reach ultimate purity, did not reach the ultimate holy life, did not reach the completion of the ultimate holy life. At that time, I had not departed from birth, old age, sickness, death, lamentation, grief, and sorrow, and had not yet been able to attain liberation from all suffering.

"Householder! Now I have appeared in the world as the Tathāgata, Worthy One, Perfectly Enlightened One, Accomplished in Knowledge and Conduct, Well-Gone One, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer and Guide of Dharma, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called Buddha, the World-Honored One. I now benefit myself and also benefit others, benefit many people, have compassion for the world, and for the sake of gods and humans seek meaning, benefit, peace, and happiness. The Dharma I now teach has reached the ultimate, reached ultimate purity, reached the ultimate holy life, reached the completion of the ultimate holy life. I have now departed from birth, old age, sickness, death, lamentation, grief, and sorrow. I have now attained liberation from all suffering."

Thus spoke the Buddha. The householder Sudatta and the bhikṣus, hearing what the Buddha had said, rejoiced and practiced accordingly.

## (156) Sūtra on the Brahmin Pārāyaṇa, Fifth in the Brahmin Chapter

Thus have I heard:

At one time, the Buddha was traveling in Śrāvastī, staying in the Jeta Grove in Anāthapiṇḍada's Park.

At that time, a great number of brahmins of the country of Kosala, in the afternoon, were wandering about and went to the Buddha. After exchanging greetings with one another, they sat to one side and addressed him: "Gautama! We wish to ask something. Will you permit us to ask?"

The World-Honored One said: "Ask whatever you wish."

At that time, the brahmins asked: "Gautama! Are there brahmins today who practice the ancient brahmin dharmas, or have they transgressed the ancient brahmin dharmas?"

The World-Honored One answered: "Today there are no brahmins who practice the ancient brahmin dharmas. Brahmins have long since transgressed the ancient brahmin dharmas."

At that time, the brahmins asked: "Gautama! How is it that today there are no brahmins who practice the ancient brahmin dharmas? How long has it been since brahmins transgressed the ancient brahmin dharmas?"

At that time, the World-Honored One answered with verses:

"Those called brahmins of old
Were self-controlled, practiced austerity,
Abandoned the five sense-pleasures,
And practiced the pure holy life.

The holy life, the precepts and conduct,
Led to a gentle and soft nature;
With tolerance, harmlessness of mind,
And patience, they guarded their thoughts.

In ancient times they had these dharmas,
But brahmins did not protect them.
Brahmins did not guard
Their money, wealth, and grain.

Reciting and studying their wealth and grain,
Brahmins guarded this treasury:
Garments of various colors,
Dwellings and beds and couches.

Prosperous cities and various lands,
Brahmins learned in this way;
These brahmins did not harm,
But followed and guarded all dharmas.

Going to the doors of others,
None restrained them.
The dharma of going forth from home to beg
Followed the proper time for meals.

Brahmins dwelling in households,
Those who saw them wished to give.
For a full forty-eight years,
They practiced the pure holy life.

Seeking the accomplishment of knowledge and conduct,
Such was the practice of brahmins of old.
They did not steal others' property,
Nor was there any cause for fear.

Love meeting with love in harmony,
They joined together in accord.
Not out of affliction
Did they engage in the dharma of sexual union.

Among all brahmins,
None could practice thus.
If there was the foremost practice,
Brahmins sought it with utmost firmness.

Those dharmas of sexual desire
Were not practiced even in dreams.
Because of this holy life,
They called themselves 'Brahmā, we are Brahmā.'

Knowing they had such practices,
The wise should know them.
Their bedding was thin, their clothing extremely simple;
On ghee and milk they sustained their lives.

Their begging was all in accord with Dharma.
Establishing festivals, they practiced giving.
At festival times, they made no other requests,
But only asked of themselves.

When establishing festivals and practicing giving,
They did not slaughter cattle.
Like fathers, mothers, and brothers,
And other relatives and kin,

Humans and cattle are likewise.
Because of this, happiness was born.
Food and drink gave bodily strength,
And those who rode them traveled in comfort.

Knowing this principle and meaning,
They did not delight in killing cattle.
Gentle, with large bodies,
With fine complexion, fame, and renown,

Diligently seeking their own benefit:
Such was the practice of brahmins of old.
Brahmins, for their own benefit,
Devoted themselves to proper and improper affairs.

In this present world and the world to come,
They would surely cross over this world.
But month after month passed,
And their intentions turned toward other things.

Sporting through the nights,
Adorned with beautiful women,
Fine cattle gathered before them,
And maidens of extreme beauty.

The subtle pleasures of the human world
Were the constant wish of brahmins.
Complete with carriages and their equipment,
Well-made, sewn, and repaired,

Households and marriages:
These were the constant wish of brahmins.
They created these bonds,
And we have come from them.

'O great king, establish festivals and give,
Do not lose your wealth and profit!
With abundant possessions, rice, and grain,
And whatever other money and wealth,

O great king, be generous in this!'
Brahmins, with chariots and vehicles,
Elephants for festivals and horses for festivals,
Horse festivals with unobstructed gates,

Gathered together for festival offerings,
Wealth and goods were given to brahmins.
From this they obtained profit,
Loving and cherishing their possessions.

From this, desire arose in them,
And craving increased again and again,
Like the waters of a vast pool,
And immeasurable wealth and goods.

Thus people had cattle,
And means for livelihood in each birth.
They created these bonds,
And we have come from them.

'O great king, establish festivals and give,
Do not lose your wealth and profit!
With abundant possessions, rice, and grain,
And if you have many cattle,

O great king, be generous in this!'
Brahmins, with chariots and vehicles,
Immeasurable hundreds of thousands of cattle,
Were slaughtered for the sake of festivals.

With horns that had done no harm,
Cattle were equal to pigs in ancient times.
They went and seized the cattle by the horns,
And with sharp knives slaughtered the cattle.

They called out 'Cattle!' and called out 'Father!',
And rākṣasas they called 'fragrant.'
When they called out these unlawful things,
At the time of piercing cattle with knives,

This dharma was practiced at festivals,
Transgressing and surpassing all that came before.
There was killing without cause,
Far removed from the dharma of decline.

In ancient times there were three diseases:
Desire, lack of appetite,
And hatred of cattle:
From these, ninety-eight diseases arose.

Thus this strife increased,
And therefore was detested by the wise.
If people see things as they are,
Who would not be disgusted?

Thus does this world practice:
Without wisdom, in the lowest of ways.
Each one despises the other out of desire;
Wives slander their husbands.

Kṣatriya women and brahmin women
Also guard their lineages.
If they violate the dharma of life,
Self-indulgence follows from desire."

"Thus, brahmins, today there are no brahmins who practice the ancient brahmin dharmas. It has been this long since brahmins transgressed the ancient brahmin dharmas."

Thereupon, the many brahmins of the country of Kosala addressed him: "World-Honored One! We have understood. Well-Gone One! We have comprehended. World-Honored One! We now take refuge in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha of bhikṣus. We humbly request that the World-Honored One accept us as upāsakas. From this day forward, for the rest of our lives, we take refuge until the end of our lives."

Thus spoke the Buddha. Those many brahmins of the country of Kosala and the bhikṣus, hearing what the Buddha had said, rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
