## (170) Sūtra on the Parrot, Ninth of the Chapter on Fundamental Distinctions

Thus have I heard:

At one time, the Buddha was traveling in Śrāvastī, staying in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's Park.

At that time, the World-Honored One, having passed the night, at early dawn donned his robes and took up his bowl to enter Śrāvastī to beg for food. While begging for food, he went to the house of the young brahmin Todeyya-putta ("Parrot," the son of Todeyya). At that time, the young brahmin Todeyya-putta had gone out on some small errand and was not at home. At that time, in the house of the young brahmin Todeyya-putta there was a white dog, eating from a golden bowl upon a large bed. The white dog saw the Buddha coming from afar, and upon seeing him, began to bark. The World-Honored One said to the white dog: "You should not behave this way, going from growling to barking." When the white dog heard this, it became extremely angry, came down from the bed, went over beside a pile of wood, and lay down in sorrow and distress.

When the young brahmin Todeyya-putta later returned home, he saw his white dog in a state of extreme anger, having come down from the bed, lying sorrowfully and distressed beside the pile of wood. He asked his household servants: "Who has disturbed and annoyed my dog, making it so extremely angry that it came down from the bed and is lying in sorrow and distress beside the pile of wood?"

The household servants replied: "None of us have disturbed or annoyed the white dog, making it so angry that it came down from the bed to lie sorrowfully beside the pile of wood. Young sir, you should know that today the ascetic Gotama came here to beg for food. The white dog saw him and chased after him, barking. The ascetic Gotama said to the white dog: 'You should not behave this way, going from growling to barking.' Because of this, young sir, the white dog became extremely angry, came down from the bed, and went to lie in sorrow and distress beside the pile of wood."

When the young brahmin Todeyya-putta heard this, he became greatly enraged. He wished to slander the World-Honored One, wished to defame the World-Honored One, wished to bring down the World-Honored One. With such intentions to slander, defame, and bring down the ascetic Gotama, he departed from Śrāvastī and went to the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's Park.

At that time, the World-Honored One was surrounded by a boundless great assembly, front and back, and was teaching the Dharma for them. The World-Honored One saw the young brahmin Todeyya-putta coming from afar and addressed the bhikṣus: "Do you see the young brahmin Todeyya-putta coming?"

They replied: "Yes, we see him."

The World-Honored One said: "If the young brahmin Todeyya-putta were to die right now, in the time it takes to bend and extend an arm, he would certainly be born in hell. Why is this? Because he is extremely angry toward me. If any being, because of an angry mind, at the breaking up of the body and the end of life, will certainly go to an evil destination and be born in hell."

Then the young brahmin Todeyya-putta approached the Buddha and said to the World-Honored One: "Ascetic Gotama! Did you come to my house today to beg for food?"

The World-Honored One replied: "I went to your house today to beg for food."

"Gotama! What did you say to my white dog that made it so extremely angry that it came down from the bed and went to lie in sorrow and distress beside the pile of wood?"

The World-Honored One replied: "Today at early dawn, I donned my robes and took up my bowl to enter Śrāvastī to beg for food. Going from house to house, I came to your house to beg for food. Then the white dog saw me coming from afar, and upon seeing me, barked. I said to the white dog: 'You should not behave this way, going from growling to barking.' Therefore the white dog became extremely angry, came down from the bed, and went to lie in sorrow and distress beside the pile of wood."

The young brahmin Todeyya-putta asked the World-Honored One: "In a previous life, what was the white dog to me?"

The World-Honored One said: "Stop, stop, young sir! Do not ask me this. If you hear it, it will certainly displease you."

The young brahmin Todeyya-putta asked the World-Honored One a second and third time: "In a previous life, what was the white dog to me?"

The World-Honored One also told him a second and third time: "Stop, stop, young sir! Do not ask me this. If you hear it, it will certainly displease you."

The World-Honored One then further said to the young brahmin: "You have asked me three times without stopping. Young sir, you should know that the white dog, in its previous life, was your father, named Todeyya."

When the young brahmin Todeyya-putta heard these words, he became even more furious. He wished to slander the World-Honored One, wished to defame the World-Honored One, wished to bring down the World-Honored One. With such intentions to slander, defame, and bring down the ascetic Gotama, he said to the World-Honored One: "My father Todeyya greatly practiced giving and performed great sacrificial offerings. At the breaking up of his body and the end of his life, he was surely reborn in the Brahmā heaven. For what cause and what reason would he be reborn among such lowly dogs?"

The World-Honored One said: "Your father Todeyya, because of this excessive pride, was therefore reborn among lowly dogs.

"A brahmin with excessive pride, after death is born in six places:
As a chicken, a dog, a pig, or a jackal;
As a donkey, the fifth; or in hell, the sixth.

"Young brahmin Todeyya-putta! If you do not believe what I have said, you may return home and say to the white dog: 'If in a previous life you were my father, then white dog, you should go back up onto the large bed.' Young sir, the white dog will certainly get back up onto the bed. 'If in a previous life you were my father, then white dog, you should eat again from the golden bowl.' Young sir, the white dog will certainly eat again from the golden bowl. 'If in a previous life you were my father, then show me where the gold, silver, crystal, and precious treasures were hidden, those places that I do not know about.' Young sir, the white dog will certainly show you the places where gold, silver, crystal, and precious treasures were previously hidden, those places that you do not know about."

Then the young brahmin Todeyya-putta, having heard what the Buddha said, received it well, memorized it, and having circumambulated the World-Honored One, returned to his home. He said to the white dog: "If in a previous life you were my father, then white dog, you should go back up onto the large bed." The white dog immediately went back up onto the large bed. "If in a previous life you were my father, then white dog, you should eat again from the golden bowl." The white dog immediately ate again from the golden bowl. "If in a previous life you were my father, then show me where my father originally hid the gold, silver, crystal, and precious treasures, those places that I do not know about." The white dog immediately came down from the bed, went to the place where it had dwelt in its previous life, and with its mouth and paws dug at the four legs of the bed. The young brahmin Todeyya-putta then obtained a great quantity of treasure from that place.

Then the young brahmin Todeyya-putta, having obtained the treasure, was extremely delighted. He placed his right knee on the ground, joined his palms facing toward the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's Park, and three times raised his voice to praise the World-Honored One: "What the ascetic Gotama says is not false! What the ascetic Gotama says is true! What the ascetic Gotama says is in accordance with reality!" Having praised three times, he departed from Śrāvastī and went to the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's Park.

At that time, the World-Honored One was surrounded by a boundless great assembly, front and back, and was teaching the Dharma for them. The World-Honored One saw the young brahmin Todeyya-putta coming from afar and addressed the bhikṣus: "Do you see the young brahmin Todeyya-putta coming?"

They replied: "Yes, we see him."

The World-Honored One said: "If the young brahmin Todeyya-putta were to die right now, in the time it takes to bend and extend an arm, he would certainly go to a good destination. Why is this? Because he has an extremely wholesome mind toward me. If any being, because of a wholesome mind, at the breaking up of the body and the end of life, will certainly go to a good destination and be born among the heavens."

At that time, the young brahmin Todeyya-putta approached the Buddha, and they exchanged greetings with each other. He sat down to one side. The World-Honored One said: "How is it, young sir? Was what I said about the white dog true or not true?"

The young brahmin Todeyya-putta said: "Gotama! It is truly as you said. Gotama! I wish to ask a further question. If you will allow it, I will dare to present it."

The World-Honored One said: "Ask whatever you wish."

"Gotama! For what cause and what reason do beings who all receive human bodies have high and low stations, have the excellent and the not excellent? Why is this? Gotama! I see those with short lives and those with long lives. I see those with many illnesses and those with few illnesses. I see those who are not handsome and those who are handsome. I see those without majesty and those with majesty. I see those born in lowly families and those born in noble families. I see those without wealth and those with wealth. I see those with bad wisdom and those with good wisdom."

The World-Honored One replied: "Those beings, because of their own actions, receive the fruits of their actions. Conditioned by actions, dependent on actions, established in actions, beings follow their high or low stations, the excellent or the not excellent."

The young brahmin Todeyya-putta said to the World-Honored One: "What the ascetic Gotama has said is extremely brief, without detailed explanation. I cannot understand it. I wish the ascetic Gotama would explain it to me in detail, so that I may understand the meaning."

The World-Honored One said: "Young sir, listen carefully, reflect well upon it, and I shall explain it to you in detail."

The young brahmin Todeyya-putta said: "Yes, I shall receive the teaching and listen."

The Buddha said: "Young sir, for what cause and what reason do men and women have extremely short lives? If there are men or women who kill living beings, who are fierce and evil, extremely wicked and bloodthirsty, who harbor harmful intentions and cling to evil, who have no compassionate mind toward all beings, even down to insects; having undertaken this action and having completed it, at the breaking up of the body and the end of life, they will certainly go to an evil destination and be born in hell. When they come to be born among humans, their lives will be extremely short. Why is this? This is the path that leads to receiving a short life, namely, men and women who kill living beings, who are fierce and evil, extremely wicked and bloodthirsty. Young sir, you should know that this action has such a result. Young sir, for what cause and what reason do men and women have extremely long lives? If there are men or women who abandon killing and abstain from killing, who cast aside the knife and the staff, who have a sense of shame and conscience, who have a compassionate mind and benefit all beings, even down to insects; having undertaken this action and having completed it, at the breaking up of the body and the end of life, they will certainly ascend to a good destination and be born among the heavens. When they come to be born among humans, their lives will be extremely long. Why is this? This is the path that leads to receiving a long life, namely, men and women who abandon killing and abstain from killing. Young sir, you should know that this action has such a result.

"Young sir, for what cause and what reason do men and women have many illnesses? If there are men or women who harm and annoy living beings, who strike them with fists, or with wood and stones, or with knives and staffs, harming and annoying living beings; having undertaken this action and having completed it, at the breaking up of the body and the end of life, they will certainly go to an evil destination and be born in hell. When they come to be born among humans, they will have many illnesses. Why is this? This is the path that leads to receiving many illnesses, namely, men and women who harm and annoy living beings. Young sir, you should know that this action has such a result. Young sir, for what cause and what reason do men and women have no illnesses? If there are men or women who do not harm and annoy living beings, who do not strike them with fists, or with wood and stones, or with knives and staffs, not harming and annoying living beings; having undertaken this action and having completed it, at the breaking up of the body and the end of life, they will certainly ascend to a good destination and be born among the heavens. When they come to be born among humans, they will have no illnesses. Why is this? This is the path that leads to receiving no illnesses, namely, men and women who do not harm and annoy living beings. Young sir, you should know that this action has such a result.

"Young sir, for what cause and what reason are men and women not handsome in appearance? If there are men or women who are quick-tempered and easily vexed, who upon hearing the slightest word become greatly enraged, who harbor hatred and give rise to worry, who broadly give rise to quarrels and anger; having undertaken this action and having completed it, at the breaking up of the body and the end of life, they will certainly go to an evil destination and be born in hell. When they come to be born among humans, their appearance will not be handsome. Why is this? This is the path that leads to receiving an appearance that is not handsome, namely, men and women who are quick-tempered and easily vexed. Young sir, you should know that this action has such a result. Young sir, for what cause and what reason are men and women handsome in appearance? If there are men or women who are not quick-tempered and easily vexed, who upon hearing gentle, rough, harsh, or forceful words do not become greatly enraged, do not harbor hatred and give rise to worry, do not broadly give rise to quarrels and anger; having undertaken this action and having completed it, at the breaking up of the body and the end of life, they will certainly ascend to a good destination and be born among the heavens. When they come to be born among humans, their appearance will be handsome. Why is this? This is the path that leads to receiving a handsome appearance, namely, men and women who are not quick-tempered and easily vexed. Young sir, you should know that this action has such a result.

"Young sir, for what cause and what reason do men and women lack majesty? If there are men or women who inwardly harbor jealousy and envy, who when they see others receiving offerings and reverence give rise to jealousy, and who when they see others possessing things wish to obtain them for themselves; having undertaken this action and having completed it, at the breaking up of the body and the end of life, they will certainly go to an evil destination and be born in hell. When they come to be born among humans, they will lack majesty. Why is this? This is the path that leads to receiving no majesty, namely, men and women who inwardly harbor jealousy and envy. Young sir, you should know that this action has such a result. Young sir, for what cause and what reason do men and women have great majesty? If there are men or women who do not harbor jealousy and envy, who when they see others receiving offerings and reverence do not give rise to jealousy, and who when they see others possessing things do not wish to obtain them for themselves; having undertaken this action and having completed it, at the breaking up of the body and the end of life, they will certainly ascend to a good destination and be born among the heavens. When they come to be born among humans, they will have great majesty. Why is this? This is the path that leads to receiving majesty, namely, men and women who do not harbor jealousy and envy. Young sir, you should know that this action has such a result.

"Young sir, for what cause and what reason are men and women born in lowly families? If there are men or women who are arrogant and greatly conceited, who do not show respect to those worthy of respect, do not show reverence to those worthy of reverence, do not honor those worthy of honor, do not serve those worthy of service, do not make offerings to those worthy of offerings, do not yield the path to those worthy of having the path yielded, do not offer a seat to those worthy of being offered a seat, do not join their palms, bow, pay reverence, and greet those who are worthy of having palms joined, bowed to, paid reverence, and greeted; having undertaken this action and having completed it, at the breaking up of the body and the end of life, they will certainly go to an evil destination and be born in hell. When they come to be born among humans, they will be born in lowly families. Why is this? This is the path that leads to being born in a lowly family, namely, men and women who are arrogant and greatly conceited. Young sir, you should know that this action has such a result. Young sir, for what cause and what reason are men and women born in noble families? If there are men or women who are not arrogant and greatly conceited, who show respect to those worthy of respect, show reverence to those worthy of reverence, honor those worthy of honor, serve those worthy of service, make offerings to those worthy of offerings, yield the path to those worthy of having the path yielded, offer a seat to those worthy of being offered a seat, join their palms, bow, pay reverence, and greet those who are worthy of having palms joined, bowed to, paid reverence, and greeted; having undertaken this action and having completed it, at the breaking up of the body and the end of life, they will certainly ascend to a good destination and be born among the heavens. When they come to be born among humans, they will be born in noble families. Why is this? This is the path that leads to being born in a noble family, namely, men and women who are not arrogant and greatly conceited. Young sir, you should know that this action has such a result.

"Young sir, for what cause and what reason do men and women lack wealth? If there are men or women who are not givers and do not practice generosity, who do not give to ascetics, brahmins, the poor, the orphaned, or travelers who come from afar to beg, food and drink, clothing, garlands, perfumes, houses, bedding, lamps, or servants; having undertaken this action and having completed it, at the breaking up of the body and the end of life, they will certainly go to an evil destination and be born in hell. When they come to be born among humans, they will lack wealth. Why is this? This is the path that leads to receiving no wealth, namely, men and women who are not givers and do not practice generosity. Young sir, you should know that this action has such a result. Young sir, for what cause and what reason do men and women have abundant wealth? If there are men or women who are givers and practice generosity, who give to ascetics, brahmins, the poor, the orphaned, or travelers who come from afar to beg, food and drink, clothing, garlands, perfumes, houses, bedding, lamps, or servants; having undertaken this action and having completed it, at the breaking up of the body and the end of life, they will certainly ascend to a good destination and be born among the heavens. When they come to be born among humans, they will have abundant wealth. Why is this? This is the path that leads to receiving abundant wealth, namely, men and women who are givers and practice generosity. Young sir, you should know that this action has such a result.

"Young sir, for what cause and what reason do men and women have bad wisdom? If there are men or women who do not frequently visit and question others, who when there are renowned and virtuous ascetics and brahmins do not go to visit them and do not timely ask about the meaning: 'Venerable ones, what is wholesome and what is unwholesome? What is sinful and what is not sinful? What is excellent and what is not excellent? What is bright and what is dark? From what do bright and dark arise? What actions bring results in this present life, and what actions bring results in future lives?' Or if they do ask but do not practice accordingly; having undertaken this action and having completed it, at the breaking up of the body and the end of life, they will certainly go to an evil destination and be born in hell. When they come to be born among humans, they will have bad wisdom. Why is this? This is the path that leads to receiving bad wisdom, namely, men and women who do not frequently visit and question others. Young sir, you should know that this action has such a result. Young sir, for what cause and what reason do men and women have good wisdom? If there are men or women who are able to frequently visit and question others, who when there are renowned and virtuous ascetics and brahmins frequently go to visit them and timely ask about the meaning: 'Venerable ones, what is wholesome and what is unwholesome? What is sinful and what is not sinful? What is excellent and what is not excellent? What is bright and what is dark? From what do bright and dark arise? What actions bring results in this present life, and what actions bring results in future lives?' And after asking, they are able to practice accordingly; having undertaken this action and having completed it, at the breaking up of the body and the end of life, they will certainly ascend to a good destination and be born among the heavens. When they come to be born among humans, they will have good wisdom. Why is this? This is the path that leads to receiving good wisdom, namely, men and women who are able to frequently visit and question others. Young sir, you should know that this action has such a result.

"Young sir, you should know that performing actions corresponding to short life will certainly result in short life; performing actions corresponding to long life will certainly result in long life; performing actions corresponding to many illnesses will certainly result in many illnesses; performing actions corresponding to few illnesses will certainly result in few illnesses; performing actions corresponding to being not handsome will certainly result in being not handsome; performing actions corresponding to being handsome will certainly result in being handsome; performing actions corresponding to having no majesty will certainly result in having no majesty; performing actions corresponding to having majesty will certainly result in having majesty; performing actions corresponding to being born in a lowly family will certainly result in being born in a lowly family; performing actions corresponding to being born in a noble family will certainly result in being born in a noble family; performing actions corresponding to having no wealth will certainly result in having no wealth; performing actions corresponding to having abundant wealth will certainly result in having abundant wealth; performing actions corresponding to bad wisdom will certainly result in bad wisdom; performing actions corresponding to good wisdom will certainly result in good wisdom. Young sir, this is what I said before: beings, because of their own actions, receive the fruits of their actions; conditioned by actions, dependent on actions, established in actions, beings follow their high or low stations, the excellent or the not excellent."

The young brahmin Todeyya-putta said: "World-Honored One, I have understood! Well-Gone One, I have comprehended! World-Honored One, I now take refuge in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha of bhikṣus. I wish that the World-Honored One would accept me as a lay disciple. From this day forth, for the rest of my life I take refuge, until the end of my life. World-Honored One, from this day on, when entering the house of Todeyya, please enter it as you would the home of any lay disciple in Śrāvastī. May the household of Todeyya obtain benefit and advantage through the long night, and obtain welfare, ease, and happiness."

The Buddha spoke thus. The young brahmin Todeyya-putta and the boundless assembly, having heard what the Buddha said, were delighted and practiced accordingly.

End of the Sūtra on the Parrot, the Ninth.

---

## (171) Sūtra on the Analysis of Great Actions, Tenth of the Madhyamāgama Chapter on Fundamental Distinctions

Thus have I heard:

At one time, the Buddha was traveling in Rājagṛha, staying in the Bamboo Grove, the Kalandaka Park.

At that time, the Venerable Samiddhi was also traveling in Rājagṛha, dwelling in a secluded meditation hut.

Then the wanderer Potaliputta, wandering about in the afternoon, went to visit the Venerable Samiddhi. They exchanged greetings with each other, and he sat down to one side. "Worthy Samiddhi, I wish to ask you something. Will you allow me to ask?"

The Venerable Samiddhi replied: "Worthy Potaliputta, if you wish to ask, then ask. After hearing, I shall consider it."

The wanderer Potaliputta then asked: "Worthy Samiddhi, I heard face to face from the ascetic Gotama, and received face to face from the ascetic Gotama, that bodily and verbal actions are vain, and only mental action is real. And there is a certain concentration such that a bhikṣu who enters it has no sensation at all."

The Venerable Samiddhi replied: "Worthy Potaliputta, you should not say this. Do not slander the World-Honored One. To slander the World-Honored One is unwholesome. The World-Honored One did not speak thus. Worthy Potaliputta, the World-Honored One has said by innumerable skillful means: 'If one intentionally performs an action, and that action is completed, I say there is no case of not receiving its result, whether received in this present life or in a future life. If one does not intentionally perform an action, and that action is completed, I do not say that one must necessarily receive its result.'"

The wanderer Potaliputta said a second and third time to the Venerable Samiddhi: "Worthy Samiddhi, I heard face to face from the ascetic Gotama, and received face to face from the ascetic Gotama, that bodily and verbal actions are vain, and only mental action is real. And there is a certain concentration such that a bhikṣu who enters it has no sensation at all."

The Venerable Samiddhi also told him a second and third time: "Worthy Potaliputta, you should not say this. Do not slander the World-Honored One. To slander the World-Honored One is unwholesome. The World-Honored One did not speak thus. Worthy Potaliputta, the World-Honored One has said by innumerable skillful means: 'If one intentionally performs an action, and that action is completed, I say there is no case of not receiving its result, whether received in this present life or in a future life. If one does not intentionally perform an action, and that action is completed, I do not say that one must necessarily receive its result.'"

The wanderer Potaliputta asked the Venerable Samiddhi: "If one intentionally performs an action, and that action is completed, what result shall one receive?"

The Venerable Samiddhi replied: "Worthy Potaliputta, if one intentionally performs an action, and that action is completed, one must necessarily receive suffering."

The wanderer Potaliputta further asked the Venerable Samiddhi: "Worthy Samiddhi, how long have you been training in the path in this Dharma and Vinaya?"

The Venerable Samiddhi replied: "Worthy Potaliputta, I have not been training long in the path in this Dharma and Vinaya; it has been only three years." Thereupon the wanderer Potaliputta thought: "Even a young bhikṣu can defend his teacher thus; how much more so those who are senior and of highest standing!" Then the wanderer Potaliputta, having heard what the Venerable Samiddhi said, neither affirming nor denying it, rose from his seat, tossed his head, and departed.

At that time, the Venerable Mahācunda was seated not far from the Venerable Samiddhi's daytime resting place. The Venerable Mahācunda, having heard the entire discussion between the Venerable Samiddhi and the wanderer Potaliputta, memorized it well and received and retained it. He then rose from his seat and went to visit the Venerable Ānanda. They exchanged greetings with each other, and he sat down to one side. He recounted to the Venerable Ānanda the entire discussion between the Venerable Samiddhi and the wanderer Potaliputta.

The Venerable Ānanda, having heard it, said: "Worthy Cunda, on the basis of this discussion, we should go to see the Buddha and present it to the World-Honored One. Worthy Cunda, let us now go together to the Buddha and explain this matter fully to the World-Honored One. Perhaps through this we may hear a different teaching from the World-Honored One."

Thereupon the Venerable Ānanda and the Venerable Mahācunda went together to visit the Buddha. The Venerable Mahācunda bowed his head at the Buddha's feet and sat down to one side. The Venerable Ānanda bowed his head at the Buddha's feet and stood to one side.

At that time, the Venerable Ānanda said: "Worthy Mahācunda, please speak. Please speak."

Thereupon the World-Honored One asked: "Ānanda, what does the bhikṣu Cunda wish to speak about?"

The Venerable Ānanda said: "World-Honored One, you will hear now for yourself." Then the Venerable Mahācunda recounted to the Buddha the entire discussion between the Venerable Samiddhi and the wanderer Potaliputta.

The World-Honored One, having heard it, said: "Ānanda, look at the foolish bhikṣu Samiddhi, who lacks discernment. Why is this? The wanderer Potaliputta asked a question that was not definitive, yet the foolish bhikṣu Samiddhi gave a one-sided answer."

The Venerable Ānanda said: "World-Honored One, if the bhikṣu Samiddhi said this in reference to the point that all sensation is suffering, what fault would there be?"

The World-Honored One rebuked the Venerable Ānanda, saying: "Look! The bhikṣu Ānanda is likewise without discernment. Ānanda, this foolish Samiddhi: the wanderer Potaliputta was asking about all three sensations: pleasant sensation, painful sensation, and neither-painful-nor-pleasant sensation. Ānanda, if the foolish Samiddhi, when asked by the wanderer Potaliputta, had answered thus: 'Worthy Potaliputta, if one intentionally performs pleasant action, and that action is completed, one will receive pleasant result. If one intentionally performs painful action, and that action is completed, one will receive painful result. If one intentionally performs neither-painful-nor-pleasant action, and that action is completed, one will receive neither-painful-nor-pleasant result'; Ānanda, if the foolish Samiddhi, when asked by the wanderer Potaliputta, had answered thus, the wanderer Potaliputta would not even have dared to look the foolish Samiddhi in the eye, let alone ask him about such matters. Ānanda, if you were to ask the World-Honored One about the Sūtra on the Analysis of Great Actions, your faith in the Tathāgata would be even more greatly increased, and your mind would be calmed and you would attain joy."

Thereupon the Venerable Ānanda joined his palms toward the Buddha and said: "World-Honored One, now is the right time. Well-Gone One, now is the right time. If the World-Honored One would teach the bhikṣus the Sūtra on the Analysis of Great Actions, the bhikṣus, having heard it, will well receive and retain it."

The World-Honored One said: "Ānanda, listen carefully and reflect well upon it. I shall analyze and explain it to you in full."

The Venerable Ānanda said: "Yes, indeed." And the bhikṣus at that time received the teaching and listened.

The Buddha said: "Ānanda, there may be someone who does not abstain from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and so on up to wrong views. Having not abstained from these and not guarded against them, at the breaking up of the body and the end of life, he is born in a good destination, among the heavens. Ānanda, there may be someone who abstains from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and so on up to wrong views. Having abstained from these and guarded against them, at the breaking up of the body and the end of life, he is born in an evil destination, in hell. Ānanda, there may be someone who does not abstain from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and so on up to wrong views. Having not abstained from these and not guarded against them, at the breaking up of the body and the end of life, he is born in an evil destination, in hell. Ānanda, there may be someone who abstains from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and so on up to wrong views. Having abstained from these and guarded against them, at the breaking up of the body and the end of life, he is born in a good destination, among the heavens.

"Ānanda, if someone who does not abstain from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and so on up to wrong views, having not abstained from these and not guarded against them, at the breaking up of the body and the end of life, is born in a good destination, among the heavens; then if some ascetic or brahmin who has attained the divine eye, who has accomplished the divine eye, sees that person, and having seen him, thinks: 'There are no evil bodily actions, nor is there any result of evil bodily actions. There are no evil verbal or mental actions, nor is there any result of evil verbal or mental actions. Why is this? I have seen that person, who does not abstain from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and so on up to wrong views, who has not abstained from these and not guarded against them, yet at the breaking up of the body and the end of life, has been born in a good destination, among the heavens. If there are others of this sort who do not abstain from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and so on up to wrong views, who do not abstain from these and do not guard against them, all of them at the breaking up of the body and the end of life will also be born in a good destination, among the heavens.' Viewing thus is right view, and views different from this are wrong in their understanding? And regarding what he has seen and known, he grasps and gropes forcefully, one-sidedly asserting: 'This is true, and all else is false.'

"Ānanda, if someone who abstains from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and so on up to wrong views, having abstained from these and guarded against them, at the breaking up of the body and the end of life, is born in an evil destination, in hell; then if some ascetic or brahmin who has attained the divine eye, who has accomplished the divine eye, sees that person, and having seen him, thinks: 'There are no good bodily actions, nor is there any result of good bodily actions. There are no good verbal or mental actions, nor is there any result of good verbal or mental actions. Why is this? I have seen that person, who abstains from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and so on up to wrong views, who has abstained from these and guarded against them, yet at the breaking up of the body and the end of life, has been born in an evil destination, in hell. If there are others of this sort who abstain from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and so on up to wrong views, who abstain from these and guard against them, all of them at the breaking up of the body and the end of life will also be born in an evil destination, in hell.' Viewing thus is right view, and views different from this are wrong in their understanding? And regarding what he has seen and known, he grasps and gropes forcefully, one-sidedly asserting: 'This is true, and all else is false.'

"Ānanda, if someone who does not abstain from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and so on up to wrong views, having not abstained from these and not guarded against them, at the breaking up of the body and the end of life, is born in an evil destination, in hell; then if some ascetic or brahmin who has attained the divine eye, who has accomplished the divine eye, sees that person, and having seen him, thinks: 'There are evil bodily actions, and there is a result of evil bodily actions. There are evil verbal and mental actions, and there is a result of evil verbal and mental actions. Why is this? I have seen that person, who does not abstain from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and so on up to wrong views, who has not abstained from these and not guarded against them, and at the breaking up of the body and the end of life, has been born in an evil destination, in hell. If there are others of this sort who do not abstain from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and so on up to wrong views, who do not abstain from these and do not guard against them, all of them at the breaking up of the body and the end of life will also be born in an evil destination, in hell.' Viewing thus is right view, and views different from this are wrong in their understanding? And regarding what he has seen and known, he grasps and gropes forcefully, one-sidedly asserting: 'This is true, and all else is false.'

"Ānanda, if someone who abstains from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and so on up to wrong views, having abstained from these and guarded against them, at the breaking up of the body and the end of life, is born in a good destination, among the heavens; then if some ascetic or brahmin who has attained the divine eye, who has accomplished the divine eye, sees that person, and having seen him, thinks: 'There are good bodily actions, and there is a result of good bodily actions. There are good verbal and mental actions, and there is a result of good verbal and mental actions. Why is this? I have seen that person, who abstains from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and so on up to wrong views, who has abstained from these and guarded against them, and at the breaking up of the body and the end of life, has been born in a good destination, among the heavens. If there are others of this sort who abstain from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and so on up to wrong views, who abstain from these and guard against them, all of them at the breaking up of the body and the end of life will also be born in a good destination, among the heavens.' Viewing thus is right view, and views different from this are wrong in their understanding? And regarding what he has seen and known, he grasps and gropes forcefully, one-sidedly asserting: 'This is true, and all else is false.'

"Ānanda, among these, if some ascetic or brahmin who has attained the divine eye, who has accomplished the divine eye, says: 'There are no evil bodily actions, nor is there any result of evil bodily actions. There are no evil verbal or mental actions, nor is there any result of evil verbal or mental actions,' I do not accept that. If he says: 'I have seen that person, who does not abstain from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and so on up to wrong views, who has not abstained from these and not guarded against them, yet at the breaking up of the body and the end of life, has been born in a good destination, among the heavens,' I accept that. If he says: 'If there are others of this sort who do not abstain from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and so on up to wrong views, who do not abstain from these and do not guard against them, all of them at the breaking up of the body and the end of life will also be born in a good destination, among the heavens,' I do not accept that. If he says: 'Viewing thus is right view, and views different from this are wrong in their understanding,' I do not accept that. If, regarding what he has seen and known, he grasps and gropes forcefully, one-sidedly asserting: 'This is true, and all else is false,' I do not accept that. Why is this? Ānanda, the Tathāgata knows that person differently.

"Ānanda, among these, if some ascetic or brahmin who has attained the divine eye, who has accomplished the divine eye, says: 'There are no good bodily actions, nor is there any result of good bodily actions. There are no good verbal or mental actions, nor is there any result of good verbal or mental actions,' I do not accept that. If he says: 'I have seen that person, who abstains from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and so on up to wrong views, who has abstained from these and guarded against them, yet at the breaking up of the body and the end of life, has been born in an evil destination, in hell,' I accept that. If he says: 'If there are others of this sort who abstain from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and so on up to wrong views, who abstain from these and guard against them, all of them at the breaking up of the body and the end of life will also be born in an evil destination, in hell,' I do not accept that. If he says: 'Viewing thus is right view, and views different from this are wrong in their understanding,' I do not accept that. If, regarding what he has seen and known, he grasps and gropes forcefully, one-sidedly asserting: 'This is true, and all else is false,' I do not accept that. Why is this? Ānanda, the Tathāgata knows that person differently.

"Ānanda, among these, if some ascetic or brahmin who has attained the divine eye, who has accomplished the divine eye, says: 'There are evil bodily actions, and there is a result of evil bodily actions. There are evil verbal and mental actions, and there is a result of evil verbal and mental actions,' I accept that. If he says: 'I have seen that person, who does not abstain from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and so on up to wrong views, who has not abstained from these and not guarded against them, and at the breaking up of the body and the end of life, has been born in an evil destination, in hell,' I accept that. If he says: 'If there are others of this sort who do not abstain from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and so on up to wrong views, who do not abstain from these and do not guard against them, all of them at the breaking up of the body and the end of life will also be born in an evil destination, in hell,' I do not accept that. If he says: 'Viewing thus is right view, and views different from this are wrong in their understanding,' I do not accept that. If, regarding what he has seen and known, he grasps and gropes forcefully, one-sidedly asserting: 'This is true, and all else is false,' I do not accept that. Why is this? Ānanda, the Tathāgata knows that person differently.

"Ānanda, among these, if some ascetic or brahmin who has attained the divine eye, who has accomplished the divine eye, says: 'There are good bodily actions, and there is a result of good bodily actions. There are good verbal and mental actions, and there is a result of good verbal and mental actions,' I accept that. If he says: 'I have seen that person, who abstains from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and so on up to wrong views, who has abstained from these and guarded against them, and at the breaking up of the body and the end of life, has been born in a good destination, among the heavens,' I accept that. If he says: 'If there are others of this sort who abstain from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and so on up to wrong views, all of them at the breaking up of the body and the end of life will also be born in a good destination, among the heavens,' I do not accept that. If he says: 'Viewing thus is right view, and views different from this are wrong in their understanding,' I do not accept that. If, regarding what he has seen and known, he grasps and gropes forcefully, one-sidedly asserting: 'This is true, and all else is false,' I do not accept that. Why is this? Ānanda, the Tathāgata knows that person differently.

"Ānanda, if someone who does not abstain from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and so on up to wrong views, having not abstained from these and not guarded against them, at the breaking up of the body and the end of life, is born in a good destination, among the heavens; this is because, if that person had previously performed unwholesome actions, and those actions were completed, then because of his not abstaining and not guarding, the results of those actions were already received in this present life, and so he is born there. Or else it is because of a later result; therefore it is not because of this cause, not because of this condition, that at the breaking up of the body and the end of life he is born in a good destination, among the heavens. Or else he had previously performed wholesome actions, and those actions were completed; because of his abstaining and guarding, the wholesome results destined for a good destination had not yet been exhausted. Because of this cause, because of this condition, at the breaking up of the body and the end of life he is born in a good destination, among the heavens. Or else at the time of death he generated a wholesome mind, and the mental concomitants were associated with right view. Because of this cause, because of this condition, at the breaking up of the body and the end of life he is born in a good destination, among the heavens. Ānanda, the Tathāgata knows that person to be thus.

"Ānanda, if someone who abstains from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and so on up to wrong views, having abstained from these and guarded against them, at the breaking up of the body and the end of life, is born in an evil destination, in hell; this is because, if that person had previously performed wholesome actions, and those actions were completed, then because of his abstaining and guarding, the results of those actions were already received in this present life, and so he is born there. Or else it is because of a later result; therefore it is not because of this cause, not because of this condition, that at the breaking up of the body and the end of life he is born in an evil destination, in hell. Or else he had previously performed unwholesome actions, and those actions were completed; because of his not abstaining and not guarding, the results destined for hell had not yet been exhausted. Because of this cause, because of this condition, at the breaking up of the body and the end of life he is born in an evil destination, in hell. Or else at the time of death he generated an unwholesome mind, and the mental concomitants were associated with wrong view. Because of this cause, because of this condition, at the breaking up of the body and the end of life he is born in an evil destination, in hell. Ānanda, the Tathāgata knows that person to be thus.

"Ānanda, if someone who does not abstain from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and so on up to wrong views, having not abstained from these and not guarded against them, at the breaking up of the body and the end of life, is born in an evil destination, in hell; this is precisely because of this cause, because of this condition, that at the breaking up of the body and the end of life he is born in an evil destination, in hell. Or else he had previously performed unwholesome actions, and those actions were completed; because of his not abstaining and not guarding, the results destined for hell had not yet been exhausted. Because of this cause, because of this condition, at the breaking up of the body and the end of life he is born in an evil destination, in hell. Or else at the time of death he generated an unwholesome mind, and the mental concomitants were associated with wrong view. Because of this cause, because of this condition, at the breaking up of the body and the end of life he is born in an evil destination, in hell. Ānanda, the Tathāgata knows that person to be thus.

"Ānanda, if someone who abstains from killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and so on up to wrong views, having abstained from these and guarded against them, at the breaking up of the body and the end of life, is born in a good destination, among the heavens; this is precisely because of this cause, because of this condition, that at the breaking up of the body and the end of life he is born in a good destination, among the heavens. Or else he had previously performed wholesome actions, and those actions were completed; because of his abstaining and guarding, the results that had not yet been exhausted were destined to be received. Because of this cause, because of this condition, at the breaking up of the body and the end of life he is born in a good destination, among the heavens. Or else at the time of death he generated a wholesome mind, and the mental concomitants were associated with right view. Because of this cause, because of this condition, at the breaking up of the body and the end of life he is born in a good destination, among the heavens. Ānanda, the Tathāgata knows that person to be thus.

"Furthermore, there are four kinds of persons: there may be a person who has nothing but appears to have something; there may be a person who has something but appears to have nothing; there may be a person who has nothing and appears to have nothing; there may be a person who has something and appears to have something. Ānanda, it is like four kinds of mangoes: a mango that is unripe but appears ripe; a mango that is ripe but appears unripe; a mango that is unripe and appears unripe; a mango that is ripe and appears ripe. In the same way, Ānanda, these four kinds of mangoes are analogies for people. There may be a person who has nothing but appears to have something; there may be a person who has something but appears to have nothing; there may be a person who has nothing and appears to have nothing; there may be a person who has something and appears to have something."

The Buddha spoke thus. The Venerable Ānanda and the bhikṣus, having heard what the Buddha said, were delighted and practiced accordingly.

End of the Sūtra on the Analysis of Great Actions, the Tenth.

# Madhyamāgama (Middle Length Āgamas)
## Fascicle 45

*Translated by Gautama Sanghadeva during the Eastern Jin Dynasty*

### (171) Sūtra on the Divisions of Deva Realms

Thus have I heard. At one time, the Buddha was staying at Sāvatthī, in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada's Park.

At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the bhikṣus: "I shall teach you about the divisions of deva realms. Listen well and pay careful attention. I shall explain it for you."

The bhikṣus replied: "Yes, we shall listen."

The Buddha said: "There are four kinds of deva realms in terms of divisions. What are the four? There are devas among the devas. There are devas among humans. There are devas among hungry ghosts. And there are devas among animals.

"What are the devas among the devas? Those devas of the Four Great Kings' Heaven, the devas of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, the devas of the Yāma Heaven, the devas of the Tuṣita Heaven, the devas of the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, and the devas of the Paranirmitavaśavartin Heaven. These are called the devas among the devas.

"What are the devas among humans? Those people in the world who are content with what they have, who enjoy the five desires, who are endowed with the seven treasures, who have riches and wealth in abundance, with many servants and retainers, many elephants, horses, chariots, infantry, and foot soldiers, with cities and territories, parks and pleasure grounds. These are called the devas among humans.

"What are the devas among hungry ghosts? Those like Yama, the king, and other great ghost kings who have great supernatural powers, great majesty, and great blessings. These are called the devas among hungry ghosts.

"What are the devas among animals? Those like the dragon king Nanda, the dragon king Upananda, and other great dragon kings who have great supernatural powers, great majesty, and great blessings. These are called the devas among animals.

"These are the four kinds of deva realms in terms of divisions."

The Buddha spoke thus. The bhikṣus, having heard what the Buddha said, were delighted and practiced accordingly.
